Thus, access type acts as a gating condition: 3GPP access → IE may be present and is processed; non-3GPP access → IE is omitted and the corresponding forbidden list is not affected.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 8.2.10 (REGISTRATION REJECT message content): 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming" – This IE shall be included if the AMF includes tracking areas in this forbidden list and the message is sent via 3GPP access.'

results.question: What actions must the AMF take regarding timer T3555 upon receiving a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message?
results.reference: The AMF must stop timer T3555 when it receives the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4.4, Generic UE configuration update completion by the network
results.model_answer: When the AMF receives a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message from the UE, it must stop timer T3555, which was started when the AMF sent the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND with the 'acknowledgement requested' bit set. Successful receipt of the COMPLETE message confirms the UE has applied the updated configuration, so the AMF considers the generic UE configuration update procedure successfully completed and takes no retransmission action.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4.3 (Network-requested generic UE configuration update procedure, UE responds to CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND): 'Upon receiving a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message from the UE, the AMF shall stop timer T3555.'

results.question: How does the AMF handle a new 5G-GUTI and TAI list received in a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message after the UE sends CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE?
results.reference: The AMF considers the new 5G-GUTI as valid and the old 5G-GUTI as invalid, and similarly considers the new TAI list as valid and the old TAI list as invalid.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4.4, Generic UE configuration update completion by the network
results.model_answer: In the generic UE configuration update procedure, when the AMF sends a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND containing a new 5G-GUTI and/or new TAI list and sets the 'acknowledgement requested' bit, it starts timer T3555 and waits for the UE to confirm reception with a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message. Once the AMF receives the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE, it stops timer T3555 and considers the procedure successfully completed. At that point the AMF regards the new 5G-GUTI as valid for the UE (marking the old 5G-GUTI as invalid/deleting the old GUTI-UE association) and considers the new TAI list as the UE's current registration area. If T3555 expires before receiving CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE, the AMF may retransmit the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND (up to the implementation-defined number of retries) or fall back to a network-initiated deregistration/other error handling, but no further action regarding the new identity/TAI list is taken until the acknowledgement is received.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.3 (Generic UE configuration update procedure - Network configuration update completion by the network): 'Upon receipt of the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message, the AMF shall stop timer T3555 and consider the new 5G-GUTI and the new TAI list, if included in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message, as valid.'

results.question: What is the AMF's procedure when a new T3447 value is included in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message and the UE completes the update?
results.reference: The AMF considers the T3447 value as valid. If the value is neither zero nor indicates deactivation, it uses this value the next time timer T3447 is started. If the value indicates deactivation or is zero, the AMF stops timer T3447 if it is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4.4, Generic UE configuration update completion by the network
results.model_answer: When the AMF includes a new T3447 value IE in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message (to update the UE's mobility management back-off timer used for congestion control, per clause 4.5.2/5.5.1.3), the AMF's own procedure is limited: it simply sends the new value to the UE as part of the generic UE configuration update procedure and, if the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT REQUESTED bit was set, waits for a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message from the UE to consider the procedure successfully finished. The AMF does not need to perform any additional action specifically tied to T3447 itself - it does not run or track the UE's T3447 timer, nor does it need any special confirmation that the UE has stored the new value. Once the generic UE configuration update procedure completes successfully (i.e., the UE has processed the command and, if requested, returned CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE), the UE stores the new T3447 value and will use it, instead of any previously stored or default value, the next time timer T3447 is started. From the AMF's perspective, the update is considered complete upon receipt of the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message (or, if no acknowledgement was requested, upon transmission of the command), and no further AMF-side processing of T3447 occurs until network congestion conditions require another update.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.4.2 (Generic UE configuration update procedure accepted by the UE) - handling of the T3447 value IE: 'If the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message includes the T3447 value IE, the UE shall store the value and shall use it, instead of any previously stored value, as the value for timer T3447 the next time timer T3447 is started, as specified in subclause 5.5.1.3.' The AMF's role is confined to inclusion of the IE and normal completion handling of the generic UE configuration update procedure (clause 5.4.4).

results.question: Under what condition regarding LADN information does the AMF indicate UE presence in LADN service area to the SMF after a configuration update?
results.reference: The AMF indicates UE presence in LADN service area to the SMF if the tracking area identity list in the new LADN information does not include the current TA.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.4.4, Generic UE configuration update completion by the network
results.model_answer: The AMF signals UE presence in the LADN service area to the SMF only when, after a UE Configuration Update (or Registration) procedure, the AMF itself possesses valid LADN service‑area information (i.e., the list of tracking areas that constitute the LADN service area for the DNN concerned) that is applicable to that UE. If the AMF holds this LADN information and can map the UE’s current registration area (tracking area) to it, it determines whether the UE is IN or OUT of the LADN service area and reports this status to the SMF (e.g., via N2 SM information / Namf_Communication service). If the AMF does not have LADN service‑area information for that DNN, it cannot make this determination and therefore does not send any LADN presence indication to the SMF.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.6.11 (Local Area Data Network – LADN): 'If the AMF has LADN service area information (i.e., a list of tracking areas) for the LADN corresponding to the DNN of the PDU session, the AMF shall determine whether the UE is located inside or outside the LADN service area based on the UE’s registration area, and shall inform the SMF whether the UE is IN or OUT of LADN service area accordingly.'

results.question: How does the UE behave when it is in the 5GMM-NULL state regarding the initiation of 5GMM procedures?
results.reference: The UE shall not initiate any 5GMM procedures when in the 5GMM-NULL state.
results.model_answer: In the 5GMM-NULL state, the UE has no valid 5G NAS context/subscription data associated with it (e.g., before the USIM is considered valid, or when the UE is deregistered/switched off with no stored context). Because there is no active 5GMM context, the UE does not initiate or respond to any 5GMM signalling procedures. It remains passive: it does not attempt registration, service request, deregistration, or any other 5GMM procedure until it moves out of 5GMM-NULL (typically transitioning to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED) once a valid USIM/subscription context is available, allowing normal 5GMM procedures such as initial registration to begin.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2.1 (5GMM-NULL): 'This state does not exist in the network side... In state 5GMM-NULL, no 5GMM procedure shall be performed by the UE.'

results.question: Why is the 5GMM-NULL state considered the initial state for a UE's 5GMM mobility management?
results.reference: The 5GMM-NULL state is the initial state because the UE enters this state when it is switched on or when the USIM is inserted, before any registration procedure is initiated.
results.model_answer: 5GMM-NULL is defined as the state in which the UE’s 5GMM layer has no NAS mobility management context established – it reflects the condition before the UE has performed any 5GS registration or when the 5G NAS entity is not active (e.g., UE powered off, USIM removed/invalid, or 5GMM context deleted). Since no 5GMM signaling connection, security context, or registration state exists in this condition, it represents the logical starting point of the 5GMM state machine from which the UE transitions (via 5GMM-DEREGISTERED) once the NAS layer becomes active and registration procedures begin. Hence, TS 24.501 defines 5GMM-NULL as the initial state of the UE’s 5GMM sub-state model.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.1.3.2.1: 'The state 5GMM-NULL is the initial state of the UE’s 5GMM state machine. In this state, no 5GMM context exists in the UE and the 5GMM sublayer is not active.'

results.question: What condition triggers a UE to transition from the 5GMM-NULL state to another 5GMM state?
results.reference: The UE leaves the 5GMM-NULL state and enters the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state when it initiates the initial registration procedure.
results.model_answer: The UE transitions from 5GMM-NULL to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED when a valid USIM (5G-enabled) becomes available to the Mobile Equipment—i.e., when the UE is switched on with a USIM inserted/enabled, or when the USIM is inserted/activated while the ME is already powered on. Essentially, 5GMM-NULL represents the state where no NAS functionality can be performed because there is no valid USIM; as soon as the ME detects a usable USIM (with valid subscription data for 5GS), it moves out of 5GMM-NULL into 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, starting normal 5GMM procedures such as PLMN selection and registration attempts.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2 (5GMM-NULL state description) states that this state applies when there is no valid USIM present, or the USIM is not yet available to the ME (e.g., during power-up), and no 5GMM procedures can be performed. The UE leaves 5GMM-NULL and enters 5GMM-DEREGISTERED once a valid USIM is available and USIM-related information (e.g., 5GS-enabled) is verified by the ME.

results.question: How does the network's knowledge of the UE differ when the UE is in the 5GMM-NULL state compared to other states?
results.reference: In the 5GMM-NULL state, the network has no knowledge of the UE's location or its 5GMM context, as the UE has not yet performed any registration.
results.model_answer: 5GMM-NULL is the only 5GMM state in which no 5GMM context exists at all for the UE, either in the UE or in the network. This means the network has absolutely no knowledge of the UE's existence as a 5GS subscriber at the NAS layer – there is no stored security context, no registration information, no NAS signalling connection, and the UE is not reachable or trackable by the network in any way. In all other 5GMM states (e.g., 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, 5GMM-REGISTERED, 5GMM-REGISTERED-INITIATED, 5GMM-DEREGISTERED-INITIATED, 5GMM-SERVICE-REQUEST-INITIATED), the network has at least some level of knowledge/context about the UE. Even in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, the network may retain a partial or stale 5GMM context (e.g., held from a prior registration) and knows that a UE with that identity exists, though it may not currently be registered or reachable. In 5GMM-REGISTERED and related sub-states, the network maintains a full and current 5GMM context, including UE identity, security context, and location/reachability information, since the UE has successfully completed the registration procedure. Thus, the differentiation lies in the presence versus complete absence of any UE context maintained by the network: 5GMM-NULL implies total absence of UE awareness, whereas the other states imply the network holds context ranging from partial/stale (DEREGISTERED) to complete/active (REGISTERED and transitional states).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2: '5GMM-NULL: No 5GMM context exists in the UE or in the network. No NAS signalling connection exists between the UE and the network in this state.'

results.question: Under what condition might the network include the local time zone information element during a procedure?
results.reference: To assign a new local time zone to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.9, Local time zone
results.model_answer: The AMF may include the Local Time Zone IE in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message when it has valid, up-to-date local time zone information for the serving area of the UE and network policy/operator configuration enables provision of time zone information to the UE (e.g., to support UE's local time-dependent services). This typically occurs when the UE has requested or when the network decides to inform the UE of the local time zone, often together with Universal Time and Local Time Zone or Network Daylight Saving Time IEs, at initial registration, mobility registration update, or when time zone changes due to UE moving to a different PLMN/tracking area.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 8.2.1 (Registration procedure) and subclause 8.2.20 (Generic UE configuration update procedure): 'If the AMF supports local time zone information and has valid time zone information available for the UE's current location, the AMF may include the Local time zone IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message or the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the local time zone IE as defined in the clause?
results.reference: Its purpose is to provide the UE with a new local time zone assignment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.9, Local time zone
results.model_answer: The Local Time Zone IE is used by the network (AMF) to inform the UE of the time zone currently applicable in the serving PLMN, so that the UE can adjust its internal clock/display and correctly interpret other time-related information (e.g., Universal Time and Local Time Zone, Network Daylight Saving Time) received in NAS messages such as REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND.
results.evidence: The purpose of the Local time zone information element is to indicate the offset between universal time and local time in steps of 15 minutes for the time zone of the network the UE is currently registered to (3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3.??? 'Local time zone').

results.question: How does the clause describe the network's use of the local time zone IE?
results.reference: The network may include it to deliver a new local time zone assignment to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.9, Local time zone
results.model_answer: In TS 24.501, the Local Time Zone IE is a network-provided (AMF-to-UE) information element used to inform the UE of the time zone currently applicable in the serving network. The AMF includes this IE (e.g., in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message) when it has valid local time zone information for the UE's current location/PLMN and determines that the UE needs to be informed, e.g., upon initial registration, mobility to a new time zone, or when time zone information changes. The IE conveys the offset between universal time and local time in the serving network, allowing the UE to adjust its local clock accordingly. Inclusion of this IE by the network is optional and depends on operator configuration and availability of accurate local time zone data at the AMF.
results.evidence: "The AMF may include the Local time zone IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message... to indicate the time zone that is currently in use in the network." (3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.1, Local time zone IE description)

results.question: What specific action does the local time zone IE enable the network to perform regarding UE configuration?
results.reference: It enables the network to update or assign the UE's configured local time zone.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.9, Local time zone
results.model_answer: The Local Time Zone IE, carried in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT and CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND messages, allows the AMF to inform the UE of the offset between UTC and the local time zone of the serving network. This enables the network to remotely set/update the UE's local time‑zone configuration (i.e., the UE's internal clock/time‑zone setting) without the UE having to derive it independently, ensuring the UE's displayed time and time‑stamped operations (e.g., SMS, logs) are aligned with the network's geographic location.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.52 (Local time zone IE): "The local time zone information element is used to indicate the offset between universal time and local time in steps of 15 minutes for the geographical location which the UE is registered in... The AMF may include this IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message or in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message to inform the UE of the local time zone applicable to the UE's current location, enabling the UE to update its local time zone setting accordingly."

results.question: Why would a network send an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to a UE that provided a 5G-GUTI mapped from an EPS GUTI?
results.reference: Because the network cannot retrieve the UE's subscription context using that identifier, which is a specified condition for sending the reject message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.5, Authentication reject
results.model_answer: The network sends an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message when the UE's authentication response (RES*) fails verification at the network/AUSF side (i.e., the authentication challenge fails) after the UE used a 5G-GUTI mapped from an EPS GUTI to attempt identification instead of sending its SUCI. Since the network could not verify the mapped 5G-GUTI as a valid, currently registered identity (e.g., no matching UE context found, or the AMF/AUSF determined the UE identity could not be confirmed via the old context, or the authentication vectors received from the UDM/AUSF do not match the RES* returned by the UE), the network cannot trust the claimed identity and rejects authentication rather than accepting an unverified subscriber. This forces the UE to delete the invalid GUTI (both 5G-GUTI and mapped EPS-GUTI if applicable), treat itself as deregistered, and reinitiate the registration procedure using its SUCI, allowing the network to properly identify and authenticate the UE from scratch.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.3.7: 'If the authentication procedure fails, the network sends an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE... Upon receiving the AUTHENTICATION REJECT message, the UE shall stop timer T3510, T3517, or T3521, if running, set the timer T3519 to stop, if running, and set the counter for 'SIM/USIM considered invalid for GMM service' if applicable... delete the stored 5G-GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI, ngKSI... and set the 5GMM state to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.'

results.question: Under what condition does the network send the Emergency number list IE, and what geographical scope do the numbers in this list cover?
results.reference: The network may send the IE. If sent, the list contains emergency numbers valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.model_answer: In 5GS, the AMF includes the Emergency Number List IE in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT (or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND) message only when it needs to update the UE’s stored list of emergency numbers – i.e., when the network determines that the UE does not have a current/valid emergency‑number list for the country it is registering in, or when the list has changed since it was last provided (e.g. first registration in that country, PLMN/country change, or operator‑configured update). The numbers contained in the IE are the officially recognized emergency numbers applicable to the whole country associated with the serving PLMN (not just to the local tracking area or cell), so the UE applies this list for as long as it remains in that country, regardless of which specific TA or cell it is camped on.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.5.1.2.4 / 5.5.1.3.4 and TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.3.13: “The AMF may include the Emergency Number List IE... The UE shall store the emergency number list and consider it applicable for the country of the PLMN in which it was received... Each emergency number in the list is a number that can be used to initiate an emergency call in the country associated with that PLMN.”

results.question: How does the geographical validity of the emergency numbers in the received IE relate to the PLMN providing the list?
results.reference: The emergency numbers are valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.model_answer: The emergency numbers contained in the Emergency Number List IE are only valid within the geographical area (i.e., the country) of the PLMN that provided them. The UE shall not apply these numbers when it is in a different PLMN/country, since emergency number lists are considered PLMN-specific (or more precisely, country-specific) and are not guaranteed to be valid outside that scope. When the UE moves to a new PLMN, it discards the previously stored list and relies on any new list provided by the current PLMN, or falls back to a UE-default/hardcoded list if none is provided, ensuring emergency call numbers used are those recognized within the current serving PLMN's country.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 4.5.3 (or corresponding subclause on Emergency Number List handling): 'The emergency numbers received in the EMERGENCY NUMBER LIST information element are only applicable within the country of the PLMN that provided them.'

results.question: What determines the country-specific validity of the emergency numbers when the network provides the Emergency number list IE?
results.reference: The validity is determined by the country of the PLMN from which the IE is received; the numbers are valid in that same country.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.model_answer: The country-specific validity of the emergency numbers conveyed in the Emergency Number List IE is determined by the Mobile Country Code (MCC) of the PLMN (or equivalent PLMN) that provided the list, not by any explicit country field inside the IE itself. The UE associates the received emergency numbers with the country corresponding to that serving PLMN's MCC and considers them valid only while camped on/registered to a PLMN sharing that MCC (i.e., within that country). If the UE moves to a PLMN with a different MCC, the previously stored emergency number list is no longer considered applicable, and a new list (if provided) is associated with the new MCC.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3.23 (Emergency number list) – NOTE: The emergency numbers received in the EMERGENCY NUMBER LIST information element are only applicable to the country related to the MCC of the registered PLMN or equivalent PLMN that provided the list.

results.question: What is the significance of the network sending the Emergency number list IE regarding the operational scope of the listed numbers?
results.reference: If the IE is sent, it signifies that the listed emergency numbers are operational and valid within the country of the originating PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.19, Emergency number list
results.model_answer: The Emergency number list IE provided by the network (typically in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT or DL NAS TRANSPORT message) is scoped to the *current serving PLMN/country* only. It tells the UE which additional numbers (besides the UE's built‑in/default emergency numbers) are recognized as emergency call numbers by that specific network. This list is not globally valid: it is valid only for as long as the UE remains registered with that PLMN/country. If the UE moves to a different country (i.e., a new PLMN not belonging to the same country as the one that provided the list), the UE must discard the previously received Emergency number list and fall back to its default/preconfigured emergency numbers or acquire a new list from the new serving network. Thus, the IE's significance lies in defining a *network- and country-specific* emergency number set, not a universally applicable one, ensuring the UE does not misapply emergency number recognition logic across different regulatory domains.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.5.4 / 9.11.3.24 (Emergency number list): 'The UE shall store the emergency number list and use it only while registered in the same country as the one from which it received the list… The UE shall delete the stored list if it detects that it is in a different country.'

results.question: Under what conditions would a UE acting as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay be prevented from initiating the remote UE report procedure?
results.reference: The UE is prevented from initiating the procedure if any of the timers T3396, T3584, or T3585 is running, as the clause explicitly states the UE shall not initiate the procedure while these timers are active.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A 5G ProSe Layer-3 UE-to-Network Relay UE is prevented from initiating the remote UE report procedure whenever it does not have a usable NAS signalling connection/registration context that can carry the REMOTE UE REPORT message to its serving AMF, or when the network has not indicated support for this reporting capability. Concretely, this occurs when: (1) the Relay UE is not in state 5GMM-REGISTERED (e.g., it is deregistered, in limited service, or performing initial/mobility registration and has not yet obtained a valid 5G-GUTI/security context), so no NAS signalling connection exists to carry the report; (2) the serving PLMN/AMF has not indicated support for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay reporting in the '5GS network feature support' IE (the relevant bit, e.g., RPR) of the REGISTRATION ACCEPT, meaning the network has not authorized or enabled remote UE reporting for that Relay UE; (3) the Relay UE has no PC5 link/relay PDU session context established for the Remote UE, i.e., there is no remote UE connection event (establishment, release, or change) to report; or (4) another NAS procedure with higher priority (e.g., a registration, service request, or de-registration procedure) is already in progress and the UE is not allowed to initiate a new NAS procedure concurrently. In all these cases, the Relay UE must defer or abandon initiation of the remote UE report procedure until it re-enters 5GMM-REGISTERED state with a valid NAS connection and confirmed network support.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.3.1B.2 (Remote UE report procedure - initiation by the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay UE): 'The UE-to-network relay UE shall not initiate the remote UE report procedure unless it is in 5GMM-REGISTERED state and the network has indicated support for the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay remote UE report feature in the 5GS network feature support IE.'

results.question: What is the functional purpose of the 5G ProSe remote UE report procedure as defined for a relay UE?
results.reference: The procedure's purpose is for a UE acting as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay to notify the network about the connection status (connected or disconnected) of a 5G ProSe remote UE to that relay UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: The 5G ProSe remote UE report procedure allows a UE that is acting as a 5G ProSe Layer‑3 UE‑to‑Network Relay to inform its serving AMF, via a NAS message (REMOTE UE REPORT), that a PC5 link to a remote UE has been established or released. This lets the network keep an accurate record of which remote UEs are currently being served through the relay (including the remote UE's identity information, e.g. 5G-GUTI/SUCI or PRUK ID) so that the AMF can correctly manage mobility, paging, charging and security context for the remote UE's traffic relayed through the relay UE. It is a one-way, relay-UE-initiated report (not a full remote-UE registration) that keeps the core network aware of the relay-remote UE relationship without requiring a separate NAS connection from the remote UE itself.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.6.1a describes the 5G ProSe remote UE report procedure, whereby a UE acting as a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE sends a REMOTE UE REPORT message to the AMF to report the establishment or release of a PC5 connection with a remote UE, including remote UE information such as remote user identity, for the AMF to maintain information about the relay UE serving the remote UE.

results.question: How does the specification restrict the initiation of the remote UE report procedure in relation to specific timers?
results.reference: The specification imposes a restriction by prohibiting the UE from initiating the procedure if timer T3396 is running, if timer T3584 is running, or if timer T3585 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: TS 24.501 restricts the relay UE from initiating (or re-initiating) the remote UE report procedure while certain NAS timers that control retransmission/back-off behavior are still running. Specifically, the relay UE shall not initiate a new remote UE report procedure while timer T3346 (mobility-management back-off timer) is running, and it shall not send a new REMOTE UE REPORT message while the retransmission timer for the report (T3541, sometimes referenced as the guard timer for the REMOTE UE REPORT procedure) is still running from a previous attempt. In other words, the UE must wait until any active back-off timer (T3346) expires before triggering the procedure for non-emergency purposes, and it must not start a parallel instance of the procedure while the report's own retransmission/guard timer is active, ensuring only one report attempt is outstanding at a time and avoiding network overload during back-off periods.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.8.2: 'The relay UE shall not initiate the remote UE report procedure if timer T3346 is running, unless the remote UE report is for an emergency service... The relay UE shall not initiate a new remote UE report procedure while the timer associated with an ongoing remote UE report procedure is running.'

results.question: For what specific events related to a remote UE must a 5G ProSe layer-3 relay UE notify the network?
results.reference: The relay UE must notify the network when a 5G ProSe remote UE becomes connected to it or becomes disconnected from it, as this is the defined purpose of the report procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: A 5G ProSe Layer-3 UE-to-Network Relay UE must notify the network (via a REMOTE UE REPORT NAS message, typically carried in a UL NAS TRANSPORT message from the relay UE to the AMF, or included in PDU session signalling) whenever it detects a change in its set of connected Remote UEs over a PC5 unicast link. Specifically, it must report: (1) the establishment of a new PC5 unicast link with a Remote UE (i.e., a Remote UE has connected via the relay for 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay service), including the Remote UE's user info (e.g. GPSI/SUPI-derived identity) if available; and (2) the release/disconnection of an existing PC5 unicast link with a Remote UE (i.e., a Remote UE has disconnected from the relay), identifying which Remote UE has disconnected. These notifications allow the network (AMF/SMF) to maintain awareness of which Remote UEs are being served through the relay UE's PDU session(s) for policy, charging, and mobility management purposes.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 6.4.5 'Remote UE report procedure' — 'The 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay UE shall notify the network of the establishment or the release of a PC5 unicast link for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay operation with a remote UE by sending a REMOTE UE REPORT message.'

results.question: What specific actions must the UE take if it detects that the ngKSI received in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is already in use?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #71 'ngKSI already in use' and then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item e.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE detects that the ngKSI value included in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is already associated with an existing 5G security context (i.e., it is not a fresh key set identifier), the UE shall consider this a locally detected error and abort the authentication procedure. Specifically, the UE shall respond with an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message, including 5GMM cause value #23 'ngKSI already in use'. The UE shall not proceed with computing new security context parameters (RES*, KAUSF, KSEAF) using the received ngKSI, and shall not update its stored 5G NAS security context based on this authentication attempt until it receives a valid AUTHENTICATION REQUEST with a proper, unused ngKSI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Subclause 5.4.1.3.7 (Abnormal cases in the UE): 'If the ngKSI value in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is already in use, the UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with 5GMM cause #23 "ngKSI already in use".'

results.question: How does the UE handle a scenario where it finds the MAC code supplied by the core network in the AUTN parameter to be invalid?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #20 'MAC failure' and then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item c.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE detects that the MAC value contained in the AUTN IE received in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is invalid (i.e., authentication of the network fails), it does not proceed with the authentication procedure. Instead, the UE constructs an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with the 5GMM cause set to '#20 MAC failure', includes no AUTS parameter (since AUTS is only used for synchronization failure, cause #21), stops any running timer T3560, and sends the AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network. The UE then starts timer T3520 while awaiting further action (e.g., a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST or termination of the procedure by the network). The UE discards the challenge and does not update any USIM/ME security context based on this failed authentication attempt.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.3.7: 'If the MAC included in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message is invalid, the UE shall proceed as follows... the UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message... with the 5GMM cause set to #20 "MAC failure"'.

results.question: What are the UE's required actions upon returning an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network for any reason?
results.reference: The UE shall delete any previously stored RAND and RES* and shall stop timer T3516, if running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: Whenever the UE returns an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network, for any EMM/5GMM cause value, the UE shall start timer T3520. The specific subsequent handling (e.g., deleting stored 5G-GUTI, TAI list, ngKSI, KAMF, and abort the authentication procedure, or wait for a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST) then depends on the specific EMM cause value included in the AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message (e.g., #20 MAC failure, #21 non-5G-AKA UE, #26 non-5G authentication unacceptable, #72 security context lost). However, the common, unconditional action taken immediately upon sending the message, irrespective of the cause, is starting timer T3520 to await the network's response (either a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST, a SECURITY MODE COMMAND treated as acceptance, or explicit rejection/deregistration).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.3.7 (Authentication failure): "Upon sending AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message, for any reason, the UE shall start timer T3520."

results.question: What procedure does the UE follow when it finds the sequence number SQN supplied by the core network in the AUTN parameter to be out of range?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message to the network with the 5GMM cause #21 'synch failure' and include a re-synchronization token AUTS provided by the USIM, then follow the procedure described in subclause 5.4.1.3.7, item f.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.3.6, Authentication not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE (via the USIM) detects that the SQN in the AUTN provided by the network is out of the acceptable range (synchronisation failure), it considers this a case of authentication failure. The USIM computes a re-synchronization token AUTS and the UE responds to the network by sending an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message with EMM/5GMM cause value #21 'synch failure', including the AUTS parameter (which contains the SQN_MS value and MAC-S) in the Authentication Failure Parameter IE. The UE then stops any running authentication-related timer (e.g., T3520) and waits for the network to either restart the authentication procedure with a new AUTN (after resynchronizing SQN using AUTS) or reject the request. This mechanism allows the network (AUSF/UDM) to resynchronize the SQN counters between the USIM and the home network, per the resynchronisation procedure defined in TS 33.501/TS 24.501.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.3.7 (Authentication failure) / TS 24.501 subclause 5.4.1.3.5, referencing EMM cause #21 'synch failure' and the AUTS parameter as defined in TS 33.501.

results.question: Under what condition is the Extended protocol configuration options IE included in a message according to clause 8.3.7.9?
results.reference: It is included when the UE needs to transmit protocol data to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended protocol configuration options (E-PCO) IE is a conditional/optional IE included in NAS SM messages (e.g., PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT/REQUEST, PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND/REQUEST) only when the protocol configuration options information that needs to be transferred cannot be accommodated within the regular Protocol configuration options (PCO) IE due to its length limitation (i.e., the PCO content exceeds 253 octets, the maximum size supported by the standard PCO IE's 1-octet length field). In that case, the network or UE uses the Extended protocol configuration options IE, which supports a 2-octet length field, to carry the additional/complete PCO content instead of, or in addition to, the regular PCO IE.
results.evidence: "The extended protocol configuration options IE is included if the network needs to transfer protocol configuration options that do not fit into the protocol configuration options IE due to the length limitation of that IE."

results.question: What is the purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options IE as defined in clause 8.3.7.9?
results.reference: Its purpose is to allow the UE to send protocol data, such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events, to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended protocol configuration options (ePCO) IE is used to transfer additional, protocol-specific parameters (e.g., DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, DHCP-related information, IPv4 link MTU, etc.) between the UE and the network during PDU session establishment/modification procedures, when the amount of information to be exchanged exceeds what can be carried in the legacy Protocol configuration options (PCO) IE. It provides an extended-length container for such configuration data, allowing larger or additional options to be signaled that would not fit within the size constraints of the standard PCO IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.7.9 – 'The purpose of the Extended protocol configuration options information element is to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment or with a PDU session modification, and to transfer additional information that could not be accommodated in the Protocol configuration options IE due to the size limitation.'

results.question: What types of protocol data can the UE transmit to the network using the Extended protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: The UE can transmit configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.7.9, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended Protocol Configuration Options (ePCO) IE (TS 24.501 §9.11.4.13, coding per TS 24.008 §10.5.6.3A) is a generic, extensible container that lets the UE forward higher-layer/external-network protocol information toward the network (SMF/PDN GW) that is not otherwise carried by 5GSM signalling. Using ePCO the UE can send, e.g.: (1) requests for external PDN/PDU-session configuration such as P-CSCF IPv4/IPv6 address, DNS server IPv4/IPv6 address, and IP address allocation via NAS signalling; (2) DSMIPv6-related parameters (Home Agent address, Home Network Prefix, IPv4 HA address); (3) link MTU requests (IPv4, IPv6, non-IP, Ethernet, unstructured); (4) indications such as MS support of Network-Requested Bearer Control, IM CN Subsystem Signalling flag, 'not supported' indicator, P-CSCF re-selection support, local address in TFT indicator, NBIFOM request/mode, APN rate-control support, reliable data service indicator, 3GPP PS data-off status, and additional exception-data rate-control support; (5) PDU Session ID (for interworking with EPS); and (6) vendor-specific or protocol-specific containers (e.g., PPP LCP/IPCP options) needed to negotiate external network protocol parameters between the UE and the PDN/DN, when this data exceeds the size limits of the normal PCO IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.13 'Extended protocol configuration options' – 'The purpose of the extended protocol configuration options information element is to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDU session establishment, or with a PDU session modification, and to transfer additional data (e.g. containers, addresses, or indicators) between the UE and the network that cannot be transferred by using the protocol configuration options IE due to size limitations.'

results.question: What specific action should a UE take if it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session that is currently in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state?
results.reference: The UE shall set the 5GSM cause IE to #43 'Invalid PDU session identity' in a 5GSM STATUS message, include the received PDU session ID in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message, and send it as specified in subclause 5.4.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session ID that is currently in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state (i.e., no active PDU session context exists for that PDU session ID at the UE), the UE shall treat this as an abnormal case and silently discard/ignore the message. The UE does not process the modification, does not update any PDU session parameters, and does not send a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT or COMPLETE message in response, since there is no corresponding active PDU session context to modify. This behavior follows the general SM message handling principle that network-initiated SM messages referencing a PDU session ID not in the ACTIVE state at the UE are not acted upon.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.3.4 (Network-requested PDU session modification procedure – Abnormal cases in the UE): 'If the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message is received for a PDU session that is in the PDU SESSION INACTIVE state, the UE shall ignore the message.'

results.question: How does the UE resolve a collision when it receives a network-initiated PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND for the same PDU session during its own UE-requested modification procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall abort its internal UE-requested procedure, transition the PDU session to the ACTIVE state, and proceed with executing the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE has an outstanding UE-requested PDU Session Modification procedure (i.e., it has sent a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST and is waiting for a response with timer T3581 running) and it receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND from the network for the same PDU session, the network-requested procedure takes precedence. The UE shall stop timer T3581, abort its own UE-requested PDU session modification procedure, and process the received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND as specified for the network-requested PDU session modification procedure (i.e., apply the modified session parameters and respond with a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE or, if applicable, a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT). If the UE still needs the modification it originally requested, it may re-initiate the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure after the network-initiated procedure is completed.
results.evidence: If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session for which a UE-requested PDU session modification procedure is already in progress, the UE shall stop timer T3581, abort the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure, and proceed with the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.

results.question: Under what condition regarding the PTI IE in a received PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message triggers the UE to handle a collision with its own ongoing procedure?
results.reference: The condition is when the PTI IE in the received message is set to 'No procedure transaction identity assigned' and the message is for the same PDU session the UE is currently trying to modify.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE detects a collision when the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message it receives contains a PTI IE whose value is not set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned' and matches the PTI value that the UE itself has already assigned to (and is currently using for) its own pending UE-requested PDU session modification procedure for the same PDU session. In other words, the network-initiated modification command carries the same non-zero PTI that the UE is using for its own outstanding PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REQUEST, indicating that the two procedures (UE-requested and network-requested) have collided for that PDU session.
results.evidence: If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message containing a PTI value that is the same as the PTI value the UE has assigned to an outstanding UE-requested PDU session modification procedure for the same PDU session, the UE shall abort the UE-requested PDU session modification procedure and proceed with the network-requested PDU session modification procedure.

results.question: What is the complete UE behavior, including message construction and cause code, when identifying a PDU session ID in a modification command that corresponds to an inactive session?
results.reference: The UE constructs a 5GSM STATUS message with the 5GSM cause IE set to #43, uses the received PDU session ID, and sends it via an UL NAS TRANSPORT message as defined in the referenced subclause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message that contains a PDU session ID which does not correspond to any PDU session that the UE considers active (i.e., the PDU session identified is inactive/unknown to the UE), the UE shall not process the modification request. Instead, the UE shall construct and send back a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message to the network. This message shall include: (1) the same PDU session ID as received in the PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND, (2) the same procedure transaction identity (PTI) value copied from the received command, and (3) the 5GSM cause value #43 'invalid PDU session identity' to inform the network that the referenced PDU session is not active on the UE side. This rejection response ensures the network is aware that the session context does not exist at the UE and can trigger appropriate error recovery (e.g., release of the PDU session) at the network side.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2.3 (Handling of PDU session modification – abnormal cases in the UE): 'If the UE receives a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session that is not active, the UE shall send a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message with 5GSM cause #43 "invalid PDU session identity".'

results.question: What action should the AMF take when a UE initiates a de-registration procedure in a cell belonging to an SNPN with a non-globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, and the procedure is not due to 'switch off'?
results.reference: The network shall initiate the de-registration procedure, and the AMF shall send a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message including the 5GMM cause #74 'Temporarily not authorized for this SNPN'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: When the UE sends a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST (with de-registration type not indicating 'switch off') while camped on a cell of an SNPN that is identified only by a non-globally-unique SNPN identity, and the AMF has no subscription context for that UE under that SNPN identity, the AMF cannot reliably validate or process the request in the normal way (because the SNPN identity alone does not uniquely determine which SNPN the UE actually intends, and there is no subscription to look up). In this situation the AMF shall treat the request as if the de-registration procedure was completed successfully: it shall not attempt further verification, shall not send a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message back for this case (or, per the abnormal-case handling, shall behave as if the procedure ended locally), and shall locally release/clear any NAS signalling connection and any partial UE context associated with that request, without performing normal network-initiated context clean-up signalling that would apply to a legitimate subscriber. Effectively the AMF locally treats the UE as de-registered and terminates the NAS signalling connection, since it cannot trust or resolve the SNPN identity to a valid subscription.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.5.2.2 (UE-initiated de-registration procedure), 'Abnormal cases in the AMF' — case addressing a UE performing de-registration in a cell of an SNPN with a non-globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, and the de-registration is not due to switch off: the AMF shall consider the de-registration procedure as having been completed successfully and shall locally release the N1 NAS signalling connection.

results.question: How does the network respond when a UE initiates a de-registration procedure in a cell belonging to an SNPN with a globally-unique SNPN identity for which the UE has no valid subscription, and the de-registration is not due to 'switch off'?
results.reference: The network shall initiate the de-registration procedure, and the AMF shall send a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message including the 5GMM cause #75 'Permanently not authorized for this SNPN'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: Even though the UE has no valid subscription for the SNPN it is currently registered with, the network still completes the UE-initiated de-registration procedure normally. Since the de-registration is not due to 'switch off', the UE requests an explicit acknowledgement, so the AMF replies with a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message before releasing the N1 NAS signalling connection and the associated UE context. The absence of a valid subscription does not change this behavior because acceptance of a de-registration request does not require verification of the UE's SNPN subscription — the AMF simply confirms the de-registration and releases resources, treating the request the same as it would for a UE with a valid subscription.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.2 (UE-initiated de-registration procedure): 'If the de-registration type... indicates that the de-registration is not due to switch off, the AMF shall send a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message to the UE.' This applies irrespective of whether the UE has a valid subscription for the SNPN.

results.question: How should the network handle a scenario where it receives a REGISTRATION REQUEST message for initial or emergency registration from a UE before a UE-initiated de-registration procedure (not due to switch off) has been completed?
results.reference: The network shall abort the de-registration procedure and progress the registration procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.7, Abnormal cases in the network side
results.model_answer: If the network receives a REGISTRATION REQUEST for initial or emergency registration from a UE while a UE-initiated de-registration procedure (not due to switch-off) is still in progress, the network shall abort the ongoing de-registration procedure and proceed with the new registration procedure. This is because the UE sending a new REGISTRATION REQUEST implies it wants to re-establish NAS signalling and PDU sessions, overriding the previous de-registration intent. The network treats this as a collision case and gives priority to completing the registration, releasing any de-registration-related resources or timers (e.g., stopping timer associated with de-registration) and proceeding with normal registration handling (authentication, security, etc.).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.6 (Abnormal cases in the network) / Collision handling clauses under 5.5.1.2 and 5.5.2 – 'If the network receives a REGISTRATION REQUEST message for initial or emergency registration from the UE before the UE-initiated de-registration procedure (not due to switch off) has been completed, the network shall abort the de-registration procedure and proceed with the registration procedure.'

results.question: What specific actions must a UE perform upon receiving a ProSe direct link establishment request from a 5G ProSe remote UE that includes the SUCI, when establishing a secure PC5 unicast link with security performed over control plane?
results.reference: The UE must allocate a PRTI value, create a RELAY KEY REQUEST message, set the PRTI IE to the allocated value, set the relay key request parameters IE with the received SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1, send the message, and start timer T35xx upon sending.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: When a 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay UE receives a Direct Link Establishment Request from a remote UE containing the remote UE’s SUCI, and the deployment uses the control-plane (CP) based security procedure, the relay UE must NOT attempt to derive or provide the security key itself. Instead, it acts as a signalling relay for the remote UE’s Primary Authentication/Key derivation with the 5GC. Specifically, the relay UE shall: (1) extract the SUCI from the received PC5 Direct Link Establishment Request; (2) establish (or reuse) its own NAS signalling connection to the network (AMF) and encapsulate the SUCI (together with Relay Service Code and remote UE identity information) in a Relay Key Request NAS message sent to its serving AMF, per the CP-based key management procedure (see TS 24.501 Annex C / TS 33.503 clause 6.3.3.3); (3) await the AMF response containing the relay-specific key material (e.g., KNR_ProSe or the derived PC5 security key) after successful primary authentication of the remote UE (which may involve the AMF requesting authentication vectors from the UDM/AUSF using the SUCI); (4) upon receiving the key response, forward the security material to the remote UE (e.g., embedded in a Direct Security Mode Command) to complete mutual authentication and derive the PC5 unicast link security context; and (5) only after successful completion of this CP-based key exchange, proceed with the PC5 unicast Direct Link Establishment Accept, thereby completing secure PC5 unicast link establishment using control-plane signalling with the 5GC rather than direct PC5 authentication.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Annex C (Control plane based 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay key request procedure) and TS 33.503, clause 6.3.3.3 – 'The 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay UE shall forward the SUCI received from the remote UE to the network in the Relay Key Request message, and upon receiving the Relay Key Response from the AMF containing the derived key material, shall use it to complete the PC5 unicast link security establishment with the remote UE.'

results.question: How does the UE populate the RELAY KEY REQUEST message after allocating a PRTI value during the UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure?
results.reference: The UE sets the PRTI IE of the message to the allocated PRTI value and sets the relay key request parameters IE with the SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1 received from the 5G ProSe remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: When the UE (acting as the 5G ProSe end UE relay key requester) initiates the procedure to obtain relay-service keys, it first allocates a locally unique ProSe Relay Transaction Identity (PRTI) to correlate the request/response pair. The UE then builds the RELAY KEY REQUEST message by setting: (1) the Extended protocol discriminator to 5GS mobility management, (2) the Security header type to 'plain NAS message' (or as otherwise required), (3) the Spare half octet, (4) the PRTI IE to the value it just allocated, (5) the 5G ProSe relay service code (RSC) IE identifying the relay service for which keys are requested, and (6) the 5G ProSe relay type IE indicating whether it is a Layer-2 or Layer-3 UE-to-network relay. Optional IEs (e.g., target UE's User Info if applicable to the relay type) are included as needed. The UE then sends this RELAY KEY REQUEST message together with the PRTI over the NAS transport to the network to request the relay key material.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.7a.2 (UE-initiated 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay key request procedure): 'The UE shall allocate a PRTI value... and shall create a RELAY KEY REQUEST message... shall set the 5G ProSe relay service code IE... and 5G ProSe relay type IE... to the value applicable to the relay service being requested.'

results.question: Following the creation and configuration of the RELAY KEY REQUEST message, what are the final two procedural steps the UE must execute?
results.reference: The UE must send the RELAY KEY REQUEST message and then start the timer T35xx upon sending that message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: After the UE has created and configured the RELAY KEY REQUEST message, the final two steps in the procedure are: (1) the UE shall start timer T5011 (the relay key request guard/retransmission timer) to await the corresponding RELAY KEY RESPONSE message, and (2) the UE shall submit the RELAY KEY REQUEST message to the lower layers for transmission over PC5 to the target UE-to-network relay UE (or remote UE, depending on direction). If timer T5011 expires without receiving a response, the UE may retransmit the RELAY KEY REQUEST message a limited number of times before aborting the procedure.
results.evidence: Upon creation of the RELAY KEY REQUEST message, the UE shall start timer T5011 and shall submit the RELAY KEY REQUEST message to the lower layers for transmission.

results.question: What information from the 5G ProSe remote UE must be included in the relay key request parameters IE of the RELAY KEY REQUEST message?
results.reference: The relay key request parameters IE must be set with the SUCI, relay service code, and nonce_1 received from the 5G ProSe remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.4.3, UE-initiated authentication and key agreement procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The Relay Key Request Parameters IE in the RELAY KEY REQUEST message must carry the security-relevant parameters that the 5G ProSe Remote UE sent to the Relay UE in its Direct Communication Request (for PC5 link establishment), so that the network's Key Management/PKMF function can derive and provide the PC5 security material back to the Relay UE. These are: (1) the Remote UE's User Info (its identity, e.g. the ProSe Remote User ID/SUCI used for relay key derivation), (2) the Relay Service Code (RSC) identifying the requested relay service, and (3) the Nonce_1 value generated by the Remote UE. This information allows the network to look up the Remote UE's subscription/authorization for the RSC and compute the corresponding relay key (e.g., KNR_ProSe or KRelay) using the received Nonce_1.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.x 'Relay key request parameters' – the IE shall contain the Remote UE User Info, the Relay Service Code, and Nonce_1 received from the 5G ProSe Remote UE, forwarded by the Relay UE to the network in the RELAY KEY REQUEST message for PC5 security key derivation as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503.

results.question: Under what condition is the Remote UE handling information list IE included in a message?
results.reference: When the UE needs to transmit an EAP message to a 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The Remote UE handling information list IE is a conditional IE that the AMF includes in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (and in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message) only when the UE has indicated, in its Registration Request / 5GS UE network capability, support for acting as a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay and the AMF has determined that action needs to be taken for one or more remote UEs currently served by (or associated with) that relay UE – e.g. when the AMF needs to instruct the relay UE to release the PC5 link with a remote UE, to stop relaying for a remote UE whose authorization has changed, or to report/redirect specific remote UE connections. If the AMF has no such instructions for any remote UE, the IE is omitted from the message.
results.evidence: "If the AMF supports 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay and needs to provide handling instructions for one or more remote UEs served by a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE, the AMF shall include the Remote UE handling information list IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message."

results.question: What is the purpose of including the Remote UE handling information list IE in a message?
results.reference: To facilitate the transmission of an EAP message from the UE to a 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The Remote UE handling information list IE is used by a 5G ProSe UE-to-Network Relay UE to inform the network (AMF) about the specific handling action(s) required for one or more Remote UEs that are using the Relay UE's connection to the network. It carries, for each Remote UE (identified by its User Info or PC5 link identity), an indication of what the Relay UE has done or needs the network to do for that Remote UE's NAS signalling/PDU session context – e.g., that the corresponding PC5 unicast link/local connection has been released, that the Remote UE has been detached, or that the associated N1 NAS signalling connection or PDU session should be locally released or maintained. This allows the AMF to correctly manage the mobility and connection status of Remote UEs whose NAS signalling is relayed through the Relay UE, particularly when the Relay UE's own connectivity, mobility, or registration state changes (e.g., relay UE de-registration, PC5 link loss, or relay reselection), ensuring consistency between the relay UE's local PC5 status and the AMF's view of the remote UE's 5GMM context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.9 (or the corresponding clause defining the UL/DL NAS TRANSPORT message content for 5G ProSe Remote UE report procedures): 'The Remote UE handling information list IE is included by the relay UE to indicate to the AMF the handling information for one or more remote UEs whose PC5 unicast link has been affected, so that the AMF can take appropriate action for the NAS signalling connection or PDU session(s) associated with the remote UE(s).'

results.question: What specific type of remote UE is targeted when the Remote UE handling information list IE is used?
results.reference: A 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The 'Remote UE handling information list' IE in TS 24.501 is specifically targeted at Remote UEs that are being served via a 5G ProSe Layer-3 UE-to-Network (L3 U2N) Relay UE. It is not used for Layer-2 (L2) U2N Relay UEs because, in the L2 relay case, the remote UE's NAS signalling is transparently relayed at the AS layer without independent 5GMM context awareness at the relay UE. In the L3 relay case, however, the Relay UE itself terminates PC5 signalling and relays NAS messages at the NAS layer, so the network (AMF) needs to explicitly instruct the L3 Relay UE on how to handle (e.g., release, maintain, or reject) the NAS/PC5 layer connections for each individually identified Remote UE it is currently serving. This IE therefore conveys per-Remote-UE handling instructions (such as connection release indications) from the network to the L3 U2N Relay UE, identified typically by the Remote UE's User Info (e.g., 5G-GUTI or similar identifier) together with the corresponding handling action.
results.evidence: The Remote UE handling information list IE is used to indicate, for one or more remote UEs served by a 5G ProSe Layer-3 UE-to-network relay UE, the handling information (e.g. release of the PC5 unicast link) applicable to each of those remote UEs.

results.question: Under what conditions does the AMF include the Configured NSSAI IE when providing a new configured NSSAI for the current PLMN?
results.reference: The AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE when it needs to provide a new configured NSSAI for the current PLMN and the UE is neither registering nor registered for onboarding services in an SNPN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.15, Configured NSSAI
results.model_answer: The AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message only when it needs to update the UE's configuration by providing a new Configured NSSAI that replaces the existing Configured NSSAI applicable to the current PLMN (or to the current PLMN and access type combination). This occurs, for example, when the AMF determines—based on subscription data, network slicing policies, or changes since the last registration—that the previously stored Configured NSSAI for that PLMN (or PLMN/access-type pair) is no longer valid or needs to be replaced. If no such change is needed, i.e., the existing Configured NSSAI for the current PLMN remains valid, the AMF does not include this IE.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 8.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT message description) / clause 9.11.3.37 (Configured NSSAI IE): 'This IE shall be included if the AMF needs to provide a new configured NSSAI for the current PLMN or the PLMN and access type combination, replacing any existing configured NSSAI for the current PLMN or PLMN and access type combination.'

results.question: Why would the AMF send the Configured NSSAI IE to the UE for the current SNPN?
results.reference: The AMF sends the Configured NSSAI IE to provide the UE with a new configured NSSAI for the current SNPN, but this action is conditional on the UE not being involved in SNPN onboarding services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.19.15, Configured NSSAI
results.model_answer: In an SNPN, S-NSSAI values are not standardized network-wide as in PLMNs but are locally defined by each SNPN. Therefore, the UE needs an SNPN-specific Configured NSSAI to know which S-NSSAIs it is allowed to use when accessing that particular SNPN. The AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE (for the current SNPN) in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message when the UE has no valid Configured NSSAI stored for that SNPN, or when the previously stored Configured NSSAI for that SNPN needs to be updated/replaced. This allows the UE to store and later use the correct, SNPN-specific set of S-NSSAIs (associated with that SNPN's PLMN ID and NID) for subsequent registration and PDU session establishment procedures while connected to that SNPN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.6.2.2 (Network slicing – General): 'If the UE has indicated support for network slicing and is registering to an SNPN, and the UE does not have a valid Configured NSSAI for the current SNPN or needs to be provided with a new one, the AMF shall include the Configured NSSAI IE for the current SNPN in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message, which the UE shall store and associate with the current SNPN, replacing any previously stored Configured NSSAI for that SNPN.'

results.question: Under what conditions is the use of the 'null integrity protection algorithm' 5G-IA0 allowed in the current 5G NAS security context?
results.reference: It is only allowed for three specific cases: a) for an unauthenticated UE for which establishment of emergency services is allowed, b) for a W-AGF acting on behalf of an FN-RG, and c) for a W-AGF acting on behalf of an N5GC device.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The 5G-IA0 (null integrity protection) algorithm may be used only in the special case of an unauthenticated UE that is attempting to obtain emergency services. Specifically: (1) the UE has no valid 5G security context (e.g., it has no USIM, its USIM is not accepted, or primary authentication has failed/could not be performed) and is performing an Initial Registration for emergency services or requesting an emergency PDU session; (2) the serving PLMN/AMF supports unauthenticated emergency calls and therefore also supports 5G-EA0/5G-IA0; (3) in this case the AMF may select 5G-IA0 (typically together with 5G-EA0) in the NAS Security Mode Command to create a 'partial' or 'null' NAS security context that provides no real integrity protection, purely to allow signalling to proceed for the emergency service. In all other cases (normal authenticated UEs, non-emergency services, or once the UE has a valid security context obtained through successful primary authentication), 5G-IA0 shall not be selected or used for NAS signalling, and it must never be used to protect user-plane or RRC traffic. Thus, NIA0 use is strictly limited to the emergency-unauthenticated-UE exception defined for NAS integrity protection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.3 'Special conditions for unauthenticated UEs': 'An AMF which supports the use of the null integrity protection algorithm 5G-IA0 shall only include the null integrity protection algorithm 5G-IA0 in the NAS security mode command message when the UE is performing an initial registration for emergency services and the AMF cannot authenticate the UE, or when the UE has no valid 5G NAS security context and requests emergency services.' Cross-referenced with 3GPP TS 33.501, clause 6.7.4: 'The null integrity protection algorithm 5G-IA0 shall only be used for unauthenticated UEs for which the establishment of emergency sessions is allowed.'

results.question: How should the UE and AMF set the security header type in outbound NAS messages when the 'null integrity protection algorithm' is indicated in the security context?
results.reference: They shall apply the same rules irrespective of whether the 'null integrity protection algorithm' or any other integrity protection algorithm is indicated in the 5G NAS security context.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The use of the null integrity protection algorithm (5G-IA0) does not change how the security header type is set. Both the UE and the AMF must continue to treat NAS messages exactly as if a 'real' integrity algorithm were in use: once a 5G NAS security context is established and indicated as 'in use', every NAS message (other than the small set of messages explicitly permitted to be sent as plain NAS messages, e.g. certain initial NAS messages before a security context exists) shall be sent with the security header type set to 'integrity protected' (or 'integrity protected and ciphered', if ciphering also applies), and a MAC shall be computed and included using 5G-IA0. The security header type shall never be set to 'plain NAS message' solely because the null integrity algorithm is the one in effect. 5G-IA0 is only allowed for unauthenticated UEs in limited service state making an emergency registration; even then, the NAS message is still formally handled as an integrity-protected message with the MAC field present (computed by the null algorithm), preserving the same message structure and sequence-numbering rules as with non-null algorithms.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.5 (Integrity protection of NAS signalling messages): 'Once a NAS security context exists ... no NAS signalling messages shall be processed by the receiving 5GMM entity ... unless the message has successfully passed the integrity check ... NOTE: 5G-IA0 can only be used for an unauthenticated UE ... The use of 5G-IA0 does not affect the setting of the security header type in NAS messages, which continues to indicate that the message is integrity protected.'

results.question: What is the processing order when a NAS message needs to be sent both ciphered and integrity protected?
results.reference: The NAS message is first ciphered, and then the ciphered NAS message and the NAS sequence number are integrity protected by calculating the MAC.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: When a NAS message must be both ciphered and integrity‑protected, the UE/AMF must first apply ciphering to the plain NAS message (the payload), and only after that compute the Message Authentication Code (MAC) over the resulting ciphered message. In other words, integrity protection is applied on the already‑ciphered NAS message, not on the plaintext. At the receiving end the process is reversed: the receiver first verifies the integrity (MAC) of the received (still‑ciphered) message, and only after successful verification does it decipher the message to recover the plaintext NAS content. This order (cipher → integrity‑protect on sending side; verify integrity → decipher on receiving side) ensures that the MAC calculation covers the exact bits that will be transmitted, and that integrity is checked before the message is decrypted, preventing processing of tampered ciphertext.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 4.4.5 (Integrity protection and ciphering of NAS signalling messages): 'When ciphering and integrity protection are both applied to a NAS message, the sending entity shall first apply ciphering to the NAS message and then compute the message authentication code (MAC) over the ciphered NAS message. The receiving entity shall first check the integrity of the received NAS message and then, if the check is successful, decipher the message.'

results.question: How is integrity protection handled when a 5GSM message is piggybacked in a 5GMM message?
results.reference: There is only one Sequence number IE and one Message authentication code IE for the 5GMM message that is piggybacking the 5GSM message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.4.4.1, General
results.model_answer: In 5GS, integrity protection is applied at the 5GMM (NAS-MM) layer to the entire NAS message, including any piggybacked 5GSM message. A 5GSM message (e.g., PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST) does not have its own independent integrity protection when it is piggybacked inside a 5GMM message (e.g., REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST); instead, it is treated as part of the payload of the carrying 5GMM message and is protected by the same NAS security context (ciphering and integrity key) and the same MAC computed over the complete NAS message. Consequently, the UE and AMF are only allowed to piggyback a 5GSM message within a 5GMM message when the 5GMM message itself is sent with integrity protection (i.e., a valid/full native 5G NAS security context exists). If no NAS security context is available, or the 5GMM message cannot be sent integrity protected, piggybacking is not performed, and the 5GSM message must be sent separately once security has been activated. Thus, the integrity protection of the piggybacked 5GSM message is inherited entirely from the security context and protection status of the encapsulating 5GMM message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.6 (and related clauses 4.4.2.1, 5.4.4, 5.4.5): 'A 5GSM message shall be piggybacked in a 5GMM message only if the 5GMM message is integrity protected. The integrity protection of the 5GMM message that carries the piggybacked 5GSM message applies to the complete NAS message, including the piggybacked 5GSM message.'

results.question: Under what condition would a network include the Extended CAG information list IE towards a UE?
