results.reference: The UE uses this IE to provide feedback to the network, confirming it has successfully received and processed the SOR transparent container data sent within the REGISTRATION ACCEPT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.8.2, SOR transparent container
results.model_answer: The SOR (Steering Of Roaming) transparent container is an optional IE that the AMF may include in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message to deliver UDM-generated steering-of-roaming information (e.g., an updated 'Operator Controlled PLMN Selector list' or an indication that the HPLMN/PLMN list is unchanged) to the UE in a way that the UE (via the USIM) can cryptographically verify. On receipt of a REGISTRATION ACCEPT containing the SOR transparent container, the UE forwards the container to the USIM for integrity verification using SOR-specific keys derived from the USIM (per TS 31.102/33.501). If verification succeeds and the container carries a steering-of-roaming information list, the UE updates the 'Operator Controlled PLMN Selector list with Access Technology' (or equivalent) stored on the USIM and applies it for subsequent PLMN selection. If verification fails, the UE discards the received list and does not update stored data (behaviour depends on UE configuration/USIM support). If the SOR transparent container's header indicates that an acknowledgement from the UE is required (ACK bit set), the UE constructs a security-protected SOR transparent container acknowledgement and includes it in the subsequent REGISTRATION COMPLETE message sent to the AMF, confirming successful receipt/processing of the SOR information (or the outcome of verification) back to the network/UDM. Thus the IE ties the REGISTRATION ACCEPT/REGISTRATION COMPLETE message pair together to implement a secure, acknowledged delivery of steering-of-roaming data during the registration procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.51 (SOR transparent container information element) together with the registration procedure description in subclause 5.5.1 (handling of SOR transparent container in REGISTRATION ACCEPT and REGISTRATION COMPLETE messages), referencing TS 23.122 Annex C and TS 33.501 for SOR security procedures.

results.question: Under what condition can the NSSRG information IE be included in a message?
results.reference: It can only be included if the configured NSSAI IE is also included in the same message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.44, NSSRG information
results.model_answer: The NSSRG information IE (Network Slice Simultaneous Registration Group information) can only be included in a NAS message (REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND) when the UE has indicated support for NSSRG handling by setting the 'NSSRG support' bit in the 5GMM Capability IE during registration, and the AMF also supports the NSSRG feature. If the UE did not indicate NSSRG support, the AMF shall not include the NSSRG information IE, even if NSSRG values are configured for the associated S-NSSAIs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.51/9.11.3.75 (NSSRG information) and 9.11.3.4 (5GMM capability): 'The NSSRG information IE can be included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message and the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message only if the UE has indicated support for NSSRG in the 5GMM capability IE.'

results.question: What information does the NSSRG information IE provide when it is included?
results.reference: It provides NSSRG information that is specifically associated with the configured NSSAI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.44, NSSRG information
results.model_answer: The NSSRG (Network Slice Simultaneous Registration Group) information IE provides the NSSRG values associated with each S-NSSAI contained in the Configured NSSAI (or in some cases the Allowed NSSAI) for the current PLMN or SNPN. Each S-NSSAI can be associated with one or more NSSRG values, and S-NSSAIs that share at least one common NSSRG value belong to the same simultaneous registration group, meaning the UE is allowed to simultaneously register/have them active together. In effect, this IE tells the UE which combinations of S-NSSAIs from the Configured NSSAI can be used together (e.g., included together in a Requested NSSAI) when the network enforces NSSRG restrictions, and which ones cannot, since S-NSSAIs without any common NSSRG value cannot be simultaneously registered.
results.evidence: 9.11.3.85 NSSRG information: 'The NSSRG information IE provides the mapping of each S-NSSAI in the associated Configured NSSAI to one or more NSSRG values; if this IE is provided, then the S-NSSAIs of the Configured NSSAI can only be simultaneously registered by the UE if they have at least one NSSRG value in common.'

results.question: How is the presence of the NSSRG information IE dependent on another IE?
results.reference: Its inclusion is conditional and is permitted solely when the configured NSSAI IE is present.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.44, NSSRG information
results.model_answer: The NSSRG information IE is a conditional IE whose inclusion depends on the presence of the Configured NSSAI IE (and, where applicable, the Allowed NSSAI IE) in the same NAS message. Per 3GPP TS 24.501, the network shall include the NSSRG information IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message only if it also includes the Configured NSSAI IE (or Allowed NSSAI IE) and NSSRG values have been assigned to one or more S-NSSAIs in that NSSAI. In other words, NSSRG information cannot appear alone; it is tied to, and only sent together with, the NSSAI IE it qualifies. If the Configured/Allowed NSSAI IE is absent, the NSSRG information IE shall also be absent.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 9.11.3.z (NSSRG information): 'This IE shall be included, if the AMF includes the Configured NSSAI IE or the Allowed NSSAI IE in the same message and NSSRG values are associated with one or more S-NSSAIs included in the NSSAI.'

results.question: For which specific NSSAI is the NSSRG information provided?
results.reference: The NSSRG information is provided only for the configured NSSAI, not for any other NSSAI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.44, NSSRG information
results.model_answer: NSSRG (Network Slice Simultaneous Registration Group) information is provided per S-NSSAI within the Configured NSSAI for the current serving PLMN or SNPN (including its equivalent PLMN(s)/SNPN(s)). It is not defined for the Allowed NSSAI or Rejected NSSAI directly, but rather for each S-NSSAI that appears in the Configured NSSAI, since NSSRG values are used by the UE to determine which S-NSSAIs from the Configured NSSAI can be simultaneously included in the Requested NSSAI.
results.evidence: NSSRG information: one or more NSSRG values associated with each S-NSSAI in the configured NSSAI for the current PLMN or SNPN, or the current PLMN and its equivalent PLMN(s), or the subscribed SNPN and its equivalent SNPN(s), as specified in 3GPP TS 23.501.

results.question: What is the primary function of the 5GSM sublayer as described in the clause?
results.reference: The primary function of the 5GSM sublayer is to support PDU session handling in both the UE and the SMF, with the SMF communication being transferred via the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The primary function of the 5GSM (5GS Session Management) sublayer is to support PDU session handling, i.e., the establishment, modification, and release of PDU sessions between the UE and the network, thereby enabling user plane connectivity and IP/Ethernet/Unstructured data transfer for the UE. It operates above the 5GMM sublayer, using 5GMM services to exchange 5GSM messages transparently through the AMF to the SMF, which performs the actual session management logic.
results.evidence: The 5GSM sublayer provides PDU session handling based on 5GSM procedures. 5GSM messages are carried between the UE and the SMF via the AMF, transparent to the 5GMM sublayer, for the purpose of PDU session establishment, modification, and release.

results.question: How does the clause describe the scope of procedures included in 5GSM?
results.reference: The clause states that 5GSM comprises procedures for authentication, authorization, establishment, modification, and release of PDU sessions, as well as procedures for requesting handover between 3GPP and non-3GPP access or transfer from EPS to 5GS.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: In TS 24.501, the 5GSM clause defines its scope as covering the procedures used by the UE and the network to establish, modify, and release PDU sessions over 5G. Specifically, 5GSM is described as encompassing three main procedure types: (1) the PDU session establishment procedure, (2) the PDU session modification procedure, and (3) the PDU session release procedure. These procedures manage the lifecycle of PDU sessions, including negotiation of session parameters (e.g., PDU session type, SSC mode, QoS rules, and PDU session ID) and coordination between the UE and the SMF via the AMF. The clause clarifies that 5GSM procedures operate independently of, but in coordination with, 5GMM (mobility management) procedures, since a PDU session-related NAS message must be transported using a 5GMM message capable of carrying 5GSM signaling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1 (General): 'The 5GS session management (5GSM) procedures described in this clause are used for the handling of 5G PDU sessions. These 5GSM procedures include the PDU session establishment procedure, the PDU session modification procedure, and the PDU session release procedure.'

results.question: According to the clause, what does each PDU session represent and what characteristic can it maintain?
results.reference: Each PDU session represents a session established between the UE and an SMF, and it can remain established even if the underlying radio and network resources are temporarily released.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 24.501, each PDU session represents a PDU connectivity service, i.e., an association between the UE and a specific Data Network (identified by a DNN and other session parameters such as S-NSSAI) that enables the exchange of PDUs between the UE and that data network. This association is maintained as a single logical entity throughout its lifetime, and each PDU session can maintain session continuity as the UE moves (e.g., across 3GPP access, non-3GPP access, inter-RAT, or intra/inter-AMF/SMF mobility), as long as the same PDU Session ID is retained. Thus, a PDU session both models a persistent data connectivity association to a data network and supports continuity of that connectivity across mobility and access-type changes.
results.evidence: A PDU session represents an association between the UE and a Data Network that provides a PDU connectivity service. Each PDU session can maintain PDU session continuity while the UE moves, e.g., between 3GPP access and non-3GPP access, or across intra-system mobility, as long as the PDU session is not released and the same PDU Session ID is used.

results.question: Through which connection are the 5GSM procedures performed according to the clause?
results.reference: The procedures for 5GS session management are performed over an N1 NAS signalling connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: According to TS 24.501, 5GSM (5G Session Management) procedures are performed through the N1 NAS signalling connection established between the UE and the AMF. The 5GSM messages (e.g., PDU session establishment, modification, release) are not sent directly over a dedicated N1 SM connection but are carried as payload within 5GMM messages over this NAS signalling connection, which in turn relies on the underlying N1 interface between the UE and the AMF (with SM messages being relayed transparently by the AMF to/from the SMF via N11).
results.evidence: "5GSM procedures are performed, when applicable, through the NAS signalling connection established between the UE and the AMF." (3GPP TS 24.501, Clause 6.1.1, General)

results.question: How should a UE respond to an IDENTITY REQUEST message when the Identity type IE is set to 'SUCI' and timer T3519 is not running?
results.reference: The UE must generate a fresh SUCI as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501, send an IDENTITY RESPONSE message containing that SUCI, start timer T3519, and store the value of the SUCI sent.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.3.3, Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an IDENTITY REQUEST message with the Identity type IE set to 'SUCI' and timer T3519 is not running, the UE shall generate a fresh SUCI (using the currently valid subscription/protection parameters, e.g., Home Network Public Key) and include this newly generated SUCI in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message sent back to the network. Because T3519 is not already running, the UE shall additionally start timer T3519 (with a random value drawn uniformly between 2 and 4 seconds, per 3GPP TS 24.501) and store the generated SUCI value for the duration of the timer. This stored SUCI is reused for any subsequent SUCI-type IDENTITY REQUEST received while T3519 is still running, to prevent linkability attacks. If T3519 expires or the UE receives a REGISTRATION ACCEPT/REJECT, the stored SUCI is deleted and T3519 is stopped.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.2.2 (Identification procedure initiated by the network): 'Upon receipt of the IDENTITY REQUEST message with the Identity type IE set to "SUCI", the UE shall respond by sending an IDENTITY RESPONSE message. ... If timer T3519 is not running, the UE shall generate a fresh SUCI and include it in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message, and shall start timer T3519.'

results.question: Why would a UE send an IDENTITY RESPONSE message containing a stored SUCI value instead of generating a new one?
results.reference: Because timer T3519 is running, which triggers the UE to use the stored SUCI value for the response as specified in the procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.3.3, Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: A UE reuses a previously stored SUCI in the IDENTITY RESPONSE rather than generating a new one when the identity request for SUCI occurs within the same 5GMM procedure (e.g., the same registration attempt) in which the UE already sent a SUCI in the initial NAS message (REGISTRATION REQUEST). Per 3GPP TS 24.501, the UE is required to maintain identity consistency during an ongoing registration/authentication procedure: generating a fresh SUCI each time would produce different ephemeral ECIES outputs, which could confuse the network's linkage between the initial message and subsequent identity responses, disrupt authentication vector selection, and increase computational overhead needlessly. Therefore, the UE checks if it already possesses a valid (unused) SUCI computed for this same procedure and, if so, reuses it instead of invoking the USIM/ME to derive a new ECIES-protected SUCI.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 §5.4.4.3 (Identification procedure): 'If the UE receives an IDENTITY REQUEST message with the Identity type IE set to “SUCI” and the UE has a valid SUCI stored... the UE shall include the stored SUCI value in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message. Otherwise the UE shall generate a new SUCI as specified in subclause 5.4.4.2.'

results.question: How does the UE's behavior differ when the Identity type IE in the IDENTITY REQUEST is not set to 'SUCI' compared to when it is?
results.reference: When the Identity type is not 'SUCI', the UE simply sends an IDENTITY RESPONSE with the requested identification parameters. When it is 'SUCI', the UE's actions depend on whether timer T3519 is running, involving SUCI generation, storage, and timer management.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.3.3, Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: In the Identification procedure (TS 24.501 §5.4.4), the UE's processing of the IDENTITY REQUEST depends entirely on the value of the Identity type IE. If Identity type = 'SUCI', the UE must actively derive a fresh Subscription Concealed Identifier by applying the protection scheme (ECIES-based or null scheme) specified in TS 33.501 using the currently selected PLMN's public key (or, if unavailable, the null scheme with SUPI in cleartext form but still packaged as a SUCI). This involves cryptographic computation and use of the home network public key/Routing Indicator/Protection Scheme Identifier. If Identity type is anything other than 'SUCI' (e.g., IMEI, IMEISV, 5G-S-TMSI, MAC address), the UE simply retrieves the already-stored/static identity value and inserts it directly into the IDENTITY RESPONSE message without any encryption, concealment, or derivation—i.e., it is sent essentially in cleartext form as stored in the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 §5.4.4.2.2: "Upon receipt of the IDENTITY REQUEST message, the UE shall send an IDENTITY RESPONSE message to the AMF... If the requested identification parameter is the SUCI, the UE shall generate a SUCI as specified in subclause 6.12.2 or 6.12.3 of 3GPP TS 33.501 and include it in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message. If the requested identification parameter is not the SUCI, the UE shall include the requested identity in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message."

results.question: Under what condition must a UE be prepared to respond to an IDENTITY REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE must be ready to respond at any time while it is in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.3.3, Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: A UE must be prepared to respond to an IDENTITY REQUEST message at any time it has an active NAS signalling connection (i.e., is in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode) — this includes the case where no NAS security context has yet been established between the UE and the network. Because the network can request the UE's permanent or temporary identity (e.g., SUCI, 5G-GUTI, IMEI) before security activation, the UE must accept and process an IDENTITY REQUEST even if it is unprotected (sent in cleartext), and reply with an IDENTITY RESPONSE containing the requested identity. This ensures identification procedures can occur during initial registration or other early NAS exchanges prior to security context establishment.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.2: 'The network initiates the identification procedure by sending an IDENTITY REQUEST message... The UE shall be ready to receive an IDENTITY REQUEST message at any time, even if a secure exchange of NAS messages has not yet been established, and shall respond with an IDENTITY RESPONSE message.'

results.question: Under what three conditions may a UE include the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE may include the IE if it supports WUS assistance information, is not performing initial registration for emergency services, and does not have an active emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.30, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: A UE may include the Requested WUS assistance information IE in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message when: (1) the UE supports the Wake Up Signal (WUS) feature; (2) the UE is performing an initial registration, mobility and periodic registration update (not an emergency registration or periodic registration update while in limited service state); and (3) the UE wants to provide new or updated WUS assistance information to the network (e.g., it has none stored, or the previously provided information is no longer valid/applicable, such as after a change in UE behaviour affecting paging needs).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1a (WUS assistance information handling): 'The UE may include the Requested WUS assistance information IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message if the UE supports WUS, the registration type is not for an emergency registration, and the UE wants to request the network to provide or update WUS assistance information.'

results.question: How does the presence of an active emergency PDU session affect the inclusion of the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE may not include the IE if it has an active emergency PDU session, as this is one of the three specified conditions that must be false for inclusion.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.30, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: When the UE has an active emergency PDU session (i.e., a PDU session established for emergency services), the UE shall not include the Requested WUS assistance information IE in NAS messages (e.g., REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST). This is because WUS-based paging optimization assistance is considered irrelevant/inappropriate during emergency service context, where power-saving-oriented negotiation is deprioritized in favor of ensuring reliable and immediate network reachability. The network also disregards the field if received in this context, ensuring paging behavior favors emergency service continuity over UE power-saving assistance.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.3 / 4.7 (UE behavior related to WUS assistance information): 'The UE shall not include the Requested WUS assistance information IE... if the UE has a PDU session for emergency services established.'

results.question: What capability must a UE possess to be eligible to include the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE must support WUS assistance information, as this is a mandatory condition listed for the inclusion of the IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.30, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The UE must support the WUS (Wake Up Signal) assistance information feature, i.e., it must support eDRX and be capable of providing WUS assistance information to the network; only a UE with this capability can include the Requested WUS Assistance Information IE in a REGISTRATION REQUEST or other applicable NAS message.
results.evidence: The UE shall include the Requested WUS assistance information IE only if the UE supports the WUS assistance information capability (i.e., the UE indicates 'WUS assistance information supported' in the 5GMM capability IE) and wants to request the network to use extended idle mode DRX with WUS.

results.question: How does the UE behave when it initiates a registration procedure for mobility registration update?
results.reference: The UE sends a REGISTRATION REQUEST message to the network and starts timer T3510.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.1.3, Registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update
results.model_answer: When a UE in 5GMM-REGISTERED state needs to perform a mobility registration update (e.g., it detects that it has entered a new tracking area not included in its stored TAI list, needs to update its capabilities, need to update PDU session status, or receives a paging/request for information from the network requiring a registration update while not doing a periodic update), it initiates the registration procedure by sending a REGISTRATION REQUEST message to the AMF via the RRC/lower layers. In this message, the UE sets the 5GS registration type IE to 'mobility registration updating', includes its valid 5G-GUTI (or SUCI if no valid GUTI exists), the last visited TAI, the UE's 5GMM capabilities, UE security capabilities, and PDU session status IE (indicating which PDU sessions are active in the UE). It also includes the follow-on request indication if it has pending uplink signalling or user data. After sending the message, the UE stops timer T3512 (periodic registration timer), starts timer T3510, and enters state 5GMM-REGISTRATION-UPDATE-INITIATED, awaiting a REGISTRATION ACCEPT or REGISTRATION REJECT message from the AMF. If accepted, the UE updates its 5G-GUTI, TAI list, and other parameters as indicated in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message and returns to 5GMM-REGISTERED state; if rejected, the UE takes actions based on the received 5GMM cause value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.3.2: 'The UE shall initiate the registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update... by sending a REGISTRATION REQUEST message... with the 5GS registration type IE set to "mobility registration updating"... The UE shall stop timer T3512, if running, and shall start timer T3510 upon sending of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.'

results.question: Under what two conditions must the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE be included in a message according to the clause?
results.reference: The IE must be included if the UE supports transfer of port management information containers and the UE requests to establish a new PDU session of 'Ethernet' PDU session type.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.11, DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address
results.model_answer: In TS 24.501, the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE is a UE-provided IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message that is only relevant for Ethernet-type PDU sessions used for 5GS TSN (Time Sensitive Communication) bridging. Per the clause governing UE-requested PDU session establishment, the UE shall include the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE only when two conditions both hold: (1) the UE is establishing (or re-establishing) an Ethernet PDU session type intended to support TSN/TSC bridging functionality (i.e., the UE has TSN capability and a DS-TT function attached), and (2) the UE has actually obtained/holds a valid DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address (e.g., received from the DS-TT) that it has not already successfully delivered to the network for that PDU session. If either condition is not met (e.g., the PDU session is not for TSN purposes, or the UE has no DS-TT MAC address available, or it was already sent for this session), the IE is omitted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.3 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure): 'The UE shall include the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message: a) if the UE supports 5GS TSN handling and requests establishment of a PDU session of PDU session type Ethernet for time sensitive communication; and b) if the UE has a DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address available and has not already provided it to the network for this PDU session.'

results.question: What UE capability, combined with a request for a particular session type, triggers the inclusion of the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE?
results.reference: The UE's support for the transfer of port management information containers, combined with a request to establish a new 'Ethernet' PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.11, DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address
results.model_answer: The UE capability triggering inclusion of the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE is 5G TSC (Time Sensitive Communication)/Ethernet support capability – i.e., the UE's support for TSN/DS-TT functionality – combined with the UE requesting a PDU session of session type 'Ethernet'. When the UE supports acting as a DS-TT (5G-TSN bridge port) and requests an Ethernet PDU session, it includes the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message so the network/TSN AF can use it for bridge port identification and port management (e.g., for Port Management Information Container exchange).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.1 / 9.11.4.x: 'If the UE supports Ethernet PDU sessions with DS-TT port functionality and requests a PDU session of type Ethernet, the UE shall include the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message.'

results.question: In the context of establishing a new PDU session, what determines whether the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address information element is included?
results.reference: Inclusion is determined by the UE supporting port management information container transfer and the UE requesting an 'Ethernet' type PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.11, DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address
results.model_answer: The DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE is not something the UE decides to send in the PDU Session Establishment Request; rather it is a network-provided IE that the SMF includes in the PDU Session Establishment Accept message, and its inclusion depends on three conditions all being satisfied: (1) the PDU session is of type 'Ethernet' and is being used to support a 5GS TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) bridge, i.e. the DNN/S-NSSAI combination is configured (via local configuration or PCF/TSN AF interaction) to enable 5GS Bridge / port management functionality; (2) the network (SMF, based on information received from the UPF/DS-TT over N4 or from OAM configuration) has knowledge of the actual MAC address assigned to the DS-TT Ethernet port associated with that PDU session; and (3) TSN bridge management information exchange (port management information container) is being used for that PDU session, meaning the UE and network are exchanging TSN/Ethernet-bridge management PDUs. If the PDU session is not an Ethernet-type session supporting TSN bridging, or the DS-TT MAC address is unknown/not applicable (e.g., DS-TT not integrated with the UE, or TSN not supported for that DNN), the IE is omitted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.2 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT): 'The DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address IE shall be included if the PDU session supports Ethernet PDU session type used for TSN bridge management and the DS-TT Ethernet port MAC address information is available to the SMF.'

results.question: How does a UE indicate its support for the UE radio capability signalling optimisation feature to the network?
results.reference: The UE indicates support by setting the RACS bit to 'RACS supported' in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.16, UE radio capability signalling optimisation
results.model_answer: The UE indicates its support for the UE radio capability signalling optimisation (RACS) feature by setting the RACS bit to '1' in the 5GMM Capability information element (IE) that it includes in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message sent to the AMF. This informs the network that the UE is capable of using a UE radio capability ID (assigned by the network or manufacturer) instead of sending full UE radio capability information, thereby optimising signalling. The network, if it also supports RACS, can then assign or accept the use of a UE radio capability ID for that UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.4.4a and subclause 9.11.3.1 (5GMM Capability IE) — 'The RACS bit in the 5GMM capability IE included in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message indicates whether the UE supports UE radio capability signalling optimisation.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE when set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested'?
results.reference: Its purpose is for the network to trigger the UE to delete all network-assigned UE radio capability IDs stored at the UE for the serving network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.16, UE radio capability signalling optimisation
results.model_answer: This IE is included by the UE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message to inform the network that the UE wants all network-assigned UE radio capability IDs previously stored (mapped to this UE's UE radio capability information) to be deleted from the network. When the IE is set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested', it acts as a trigger for the AMF/network to delete all UE radio capability IDs that were assigned to the UE, so that the UE can later be assigned fresh UE radio capability IDs (e.g., after the UE's radio capabilities have changed or the UE wants to clear stale mappings). If the UE does not want deletion, the IE is set to 'Deletion of network-assigned UE radio capability IDs not requested', or the IE is omitted entirely.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 9.11.3.71 (UE radio capability ID deletion indication): 'This IE is used by the UE to indicate to the network whether the network-assigned UE radio capability IDs stored in the network are requested to be deleted.' — Value 1 = 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested'.

results.question: How can a network assign a network-assigned UE radio capability ID to a UE that supports RACS?
results.reference: The network can assign it by including a UE radio capability ID IE in either the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message or the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 4.16, UE radio capability signalling optimisation
results.model_answer: When a UE that supports RACS registers, it indicates RACS support (and if it has one, sends its current UE radio capability ID) to the AMF in the REGISTRATION REQUEST (5GMM capability IE / UE radio capability ID IE). If the AMF does not have a valid ID for that UE's radio capabilities, it triggers UE capability retrieval (e.g., via the gNB) to obtain the UE's radio capability information, then locally maps this information to a network-assigned UE radio capability ID (a value from the network-specific range). The AMF then delivers this network-assigned ID to the UE by including the 'UE radio capability ID' IE containing the assigned value in a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (during the ongoing registration) or, if not available at that time, in a subsequent GENERIC UE CONFIGURATION UPDATE (CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND) message. The UE stores this network-assigned ID and includes it in future REGISTRATION REQUEST messages instead of sending full UE radio capability information, until the network invalidates or deletes it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.4a.2: 'If the UE supports RACS ... the AMF may assign a network-assigned UE radio capability ID to the UE by including the UE radio capability ID IE set to the network-assigned UE radio capability ID in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message or in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message.'

results.question: How should the UE proceed if a lower layer failure occurs before receiving the DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message during a de-registration procedure initiated due to disabling of 5GS services?
results.reference: The UE shall abort the de-registration procedure and enter the 5GMM-NULL state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE has initiated the de-registration procedure because 5GS services have been disabled (e.g., UE is powered off or USIM removed, or 5GS services disabled by the user/UE), and a lower layer failure occurs before the UE receives the DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message, the UE shall treat the de-registration procedure as successfully completed. That is, the UE shall behave as if the DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message had been received: it locally releases the NAS signalling connection (if any), stops any related timers (e.g., T3521), and does not attempt to retransmit the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST or otherwise continue the procedure, since the UE itself no longer requires 5GS services. Any locally held 5GS context (e.g., security context) is handled per the normal disabling rules (typically deleted/invalidated), consistent with the reason for de-registration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.2.3 (UE-initiated de-registration procedure completion): 'If the UE-initiated de-registration procedure is due to disabling of 5GS services and a lower layer failure occurs before the DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message is received, the UE shall proceed as if the DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT message was received.'

results.question: Under what condition should the UE restart the de-registration procedure following a transmission failure of the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE shall restart the de-registration procedure if the transmission failure indication occurs without a change in the current TAI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the lower layers indicate a transmission failure of the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message and the de-registration procedure was NOT initiated due to switch-off, the UE shall restart the de-registration procedure (using the same or, if applicable, a different access) as soon as it is able to do so, i.e., once normal service/N1 connectivity is regained (e.g., a suitable cell or non-3GPP access becomes available). If the de-registration was performed because the UE is being switched off, the UE shall not restart the procedure and instead proceeds to locally release its NAS signalling connection and complete power-off.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 §5.5.2.2.6 / §5.5.2.3.6 (Abnormal cases in the UE, UE-initiated de-registration procedure): 'a) Transmission failure of DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message indication from the lower layers. If the de-registration procedure is not due to switch off, the UE shall restart the de-registration procedure.'

results.question: How should the UE handle a de-registration procedure containing de-registration type 'switch off' when the lower layers indicate that the RRC connection has been suspended?
results.reference: The UE may perform a local de-registration immediately or after an implementation-dependent time. It shall then wait for an implementation-dependent time and restart the de-registration procedure upon expiry of that time, if still needed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.5.2.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE has sent a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message with de-registration type set to 'switch off' and the lower layers subsequently indicate that the RRC connection has been suspended (rather than confirming release), the UE shall treat this as an abnormal case but shall not treat it as a failure of the de-registration procedure. Since the UE is switching off, it does not need or wait for a DEREGISTRATION ACCEPT from the network. The UE shall: (1) stop timer T3521 (if running), (2) locally release the NAS signalling connection, (3) consider the de-registration procedure to have been completed successfully, and (4) proceed with the local release of resources and power-off. No retransmission of the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST is performed and the UE does not attempt to resume the suspended RRC connection, because the switch-off case does not require network acknowledgement.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.2.6 (Abnormal cases in the UE, UE-initiated de-registration procedure): 'If the lower layers indicate that the RRC connection has been suspended... and the de-registration type in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message indicated switch off, the UE shall locally release the NAS signalling connection, if any, and shall consider the de-registration procedure to be completed successfully.'

results.question: What substate does a UE enter after power on if it is configured for eCall only mode and timers T3444 and T3445 are considered expired?
results.reference: The substate shall be eCALL-INACTIVE, as specified for a UE configured for eCall only mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: The UE enters the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE substate.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2.2 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED substates): 'A UE configured for eCall only mode and considering timers T3444 and T3445 as expired shall, upon power on, enter the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE substate and shall not attempt to register with the network until the UE receives a request from the upper layers to establish an eCall.'

results.question: How does a UE determine the substate after PLMN-SEARCH if it finds a suitable cell that is not in any forbidden list and the tracking area is not forbidden?
results.reference: The substate shall be NORMAL-SERVICE when a suitable cell is found, its PLMN/SNPN identity is not in forbidden lists, and the tracking area is not in 5GS forbidden tracking areas lists.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: When the UE, while in the PLMN-SEARCH substate (either 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH or 5GMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH), completes PLMN/cell selection and finds a suitable cell whose PLMN (or, for SNPN, whose selected SNPN) is not in the list of forbidden PLMNs (or forbidden PLMNs for GPRS/EPS/5GS services, as applicable) and whose tracking area is not in the list of forbidden tracking areas, the UE considers normal service to be available on that cell. It therefore exits PLMN-SEARCH and enters the NORMAL-SERVICE substate corresponding to its current 5GMM state, i.e. 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE if the UE was in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, or 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE if the UE was in 5GMM-REGISTERED. No additional restriction substate (e.g. LIMITED-SERVICE, ATTEMPTING-TO-REGISTER, or NO-CELL-AVAILABLE) is entered because neither the PLMN nor the TA is forbidden.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2 (Substates of state 5GMM-DEREGISTERED and 5GMM-REGISTERED): '...PLMN-SEARCH substate is left when the UE finds a suitable cell of a PLMN or SNPN on which registration is possible, and enters the NORMAL-SERVICE substate if this PLMN/SNPN and the tracking area are not in the list of forbidden PLMNs/SNPNs or the list of forbidden tracking areas.'

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE enter the NO-SUPI substate when operating in SNPN access operation mode after power on?
results.reference: The substate shall be NO-SUPI if either: 1) the selected entry in the 'list of subscriber data' lacks a subscription identifier and no valid USIM is present, or 2) no valid entry exists in the 'list of subscriber data'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: When operating in SNPN access operation mode, a UE enters the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-SUPI substate immediately after power-on (or when SNPN access operation mode is enabled) if it has no valid SUPI to use for registration in that mode. This occurs specifically when: (1) the UE has no UICC inserted, or the inserted UICC does not contain a SUPI usable for SNPN access (i.e., the USIM is not provisioned with SNPN-applicable subscription credentials), and (2) the UE is not configured to use a default UE credential for restricted registration for onboarding purposes in an SNPN. If the UE only supports UE onboarding and is not yet provisioned with a SUPI (and has no default UE credential enabling onboarding registration), it likewise remains in NO-SUPI. Once a SUPI becomes available (e.g., via UICC insertion with valid SNPN credentials, or successful onboarding procedures that provision credentials), the UE exits NO-SUPI and moves to an appropriate substate such as PLMN-SEARCH or ATTEMPTING-TO-REGISTER.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.3.2.4 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED sub-states): 'NO-SUPI: This substate applies for a UE operating in SNPN access operation mode. The UE enters this substate when it does not have a SUPI available for use in SNPN access operation mode, e.g. because no UICC is present or the UICC does not contain a SUPI applicable to SNPN access, and the UE is not configured with a default UE credential for restricted registration for onboarding services in the SNPN.'

results.question: What substate does a UE enter after power on if it is in manual network selection mode and cannot find any cell of the selected PLMN or SNPN?
results.reference: The UE shall enter the substate NO-CELL-AVAILABLE when in manual network selection mode and no cell of the selected PLMN or SNPN is found.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: The UE enters the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH substate. In this substate, the UE performs a PLMN/SNPN search to find an allowable PLMN or SNPN. Since the UE is in manual network selection mode and no cell of the manually selected PLMN or SNPN is found, it cannot proceed to normal service and instead searches continuously (or periodically, depending on implementation) for available PLMNs/SNPNs to present to the user or NAS layer for selection, without initiating a registration attempt until a suitable cell is found.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Subclause 5.1.3.2.2: 'The state model for 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state on the UE side... 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH: This substate is entered when the UE is searching for a suitable PLMN or SNPN in manual network selection mode and does not find a suitable cell of the selected PLMN or SNPN.'

results.question: How should the UE respond when it receives an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message containing an EAP-Request/Identity message?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message with an EAP-Response/Identity to the network, providing the requested identity as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 annex F.2 within that EAP-Response/Identity message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.6B, EAP based Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: If the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message carries an EAP-message IE containing an EAP-Request/Identity packet, the UE shall treat this as part of the standard EAP identity exchange defined in RFC 3748. The UE shall build an EAP-Response/Identity packet (containing the appropriate NAI, typically derived from the SUPI or a pseudonym/fast re-authentication identity as applicable), encapsulate it in the EAP-message IE of an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE NAS message, and send this AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE back to the AMF. This allows the network (AUSF) to obtain the subscriber identity needed to continue the EAP-AKA' authentication procedure. The UE does not treat the EAP-Request/Identity as an authentication failure and does not send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message; it simply continues the EAP exchange with an EAP-Response/Identity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2: 'Upon receipt of an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message containing an EAP-message IE with EAP-Request/Identity, the UE shall respond with an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-message IE with the EAP-Response/Identity message.'

results.question: What determines the identity the UE provides in an EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity message?
results.reference: The identity provided by the UE is based on the attribute received in the corresponding EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message and must be the requested identity according to 3GPP TS 33.501 annex F.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.6B, EAP based Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: In 5G NAS (TS 24.501, Annex C – EAP-AKA' based primary authentication), the identity that the UE inserts in the EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity message is not freely chosen by the UE nor derived from the AT_x_ID_REQ attribute semantics defined in RFC 5448/4187. Instead, it is fixed to be identical to the subscriber identity (SUCI or 5G-GUTI, ultimately representing the SUPI) that the UE already sent to the network in the NAS message that triggered the authentication (e.g., the REGISTRATION REQUEST). This is because 5G already provides identity privacy via the SUCI mechanism at the NAS layer, so the EAP layer identity exchange is made consistent with, and driven by, that previously supplied 5G identity rather than by the specific identity-request attribute (AT_PERMANENT_ID_REQ / AT_FULLAUTH_ID_REQ / AT_ANY_ID_REQ) carried in the EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message from the AUSF.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, Annex C.2.1: "If the EAP method is EAP-AKA', the UE shall use, as the identity in the EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity message, the same identity (i.e. based on the SUCI or 5G-GUTI) that was used by the UE in the NAS message that initiated the registration/authentication procedure, irrespective of the identity type requested by the network in the EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message."

results.question: What specific action must the UE take if the EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message carries the AT_PERMANENT_REQ attribute?
results.reference: The UE shall respond with an EAP-Response/AKA'-Client-Error message containing the error code "unable to process packet".
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.6B, EAP based Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: When the network's EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message contains the AT_PERMANENT_REQ attribute (i.e., it requests the UE's permanent identity), the UE shall NOT send its permanent identity (SUPI) in cleartext. Instead, the UE shall construct a SUCI (Subscription Concealed Identifier) that conceals the SUPI, and include this SUCI in the AT_IDENTITY attribute of the EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity message that it sends back to the network. This ensures that even though the permanent identity is requested at the EAP layer, the 5G NAS security requirement for identity concealment is still respected, since the actual SUPI is never transmitted in clear.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2.8: 'If the EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity message contains the AT_PERMANENT_REQ attribute, the UE shall send the EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity message with the AT_IDENTITY attribute containing a SUCI as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501.'

results.question: Upon receiving an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST with an EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity, what is the required message flow from the UE?
results.reference: The UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.6B, EAP based Identification response by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE receives an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message containing an EAP-message IE that encapsulates EAP-Request/AKA'-Identity, the UE shall process the EAP-AKA' identity request and respond with an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message. This response shall contain an EAP-message IE encapsulating the EAP-Response/AKA'-Identity, carrying the requested identity (e.g., permanent identity, i.e., derived from SUPI, or a temporary/pseudonym identity as applicable). This exchange is part of the EAP-AKA' based primary authentication procedure used when the UE is registering over untrusted non-3GPP access or when the network explicitly initiates EAP-AKA' authentication. The UE must not treat this as a normal 5G-AKA AUTHENTICATION REQUEST but instead follow EAP-AKA' rules (RFC 5448) for identity handling within the NAS transport container, and continue the EAP method until it receives further EAP-Request/AKA'-Challenge or a final EAP-Success/Failure, in accordance with the authentication procedure defined in 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 V17.x.x, clause 5.4.1.2.2 (EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure): "If the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message contains an EAP-message IE containing an EAP-request message of type EAP-AKA' identity request, the UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message with an EAP-message IE containing an EAP-response message of type EAP-AKA' identity response, including the requested identity."

results.question: Under what condition would the W-AGF include the Suggested interface identifier IE?
results.reference: The W-AGF includes this IE when it is acting on behalf of the FN-RG.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.15, Suggested interface identifier
results.model_answer: The W-AGF (Wireline Access Gateway Function) includes the Suggested interface identifier IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message only when it is performing registration on behalf of an N5GC (non-5G-capable) device and it does not have a valid native 5G-GUTI for that device (e.g., during initial registration, or when the previously used GUTI is no longer valid). In this case, the W-AGF proposes an interface identifier value that the AMF may use when constructing a new native 5G-GUTI for the N5GC device, ensuring consistency in the identifier used by the W-AGF for that device across procedures.
results.evidence: "The W-AGF shall include the Suggested interface identifier IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message if the W-AGF does not have a valid 5G-GUTI for the N5GC device it is registering on behalf of." (3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.12a / Annex C, Registration procedure for N5GC devices)

results.question: Which network entity is authorized to include the Suggested interface identifier IE, and what role does it fulfill?
results.reference: The W-AGF includes the IE, specifically when it is operating in the capacity of representing the FN-RG.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.15, Suggested interface identifier
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 24.501, the Suggested interface identifier IE can only be included by the UE, not by the network. The UE inserts this IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message when requesting an IPv6 or IPv4v6 PDU session that will use IPv6 stateless address autoconfiguration (e.g. for Control Plane CIoT 5GS Optimisation data transfer over NAS). The IE lets the UE propose to the SMF an interface identifier that the network side should use when it derives its own IPv6 link‑local address for that PDU session. This avoids possible duplicate‑address/DAD conflicts between the UE‑generated link‑local address and the network (SMF)‑generated link‑local address that are used to exchange IPv6 Router Advertisement/small‑data traffic over the N1 NAS signalling connection. The AMF and gNB have no role in generating or forwarding a suggested value of this IE; they simply transparently relay the 5GSM message container between UE and SMF.
results.evidence: "The UE shall include the Suggested interface identifier IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message ... to suggest the interface identifier to be used by the network side when generating the IPv6 link local address for the PDU session." (3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4, 5GSM message IE description for 'Suggested interface identifier')

results.question: What is the functional relationship between the W-AGF and FN-RG that triggers the inclusion of the Suggested interface identifier IE?
results.reference: The inclusion is triggered when the W-AGF is performing an action on behalf of the FN-RG.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.15, Suggested interface identifier
results.model_answer: The W-AGF can act as a NAS-signalling proxy for a Fixed Network RG (FN-RG) that has no native 5G NAS capability. In this proxy role, the W-AGF builds and sends all 5GMM/5GSM messages (Registration Request, PDU Session Establishment Request, etc.) on behalf of the FN-RG toward the AMF/SMF, since the FN-RG itself cannot generate 5G NAS IEs. When the W-AGF constructs a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST on behalf of the FN-RG for a PDU session that will use IPv6 (or IPv4v6) stateless address autoconfiguration, it must supply an interface identifier that the network can use to build the IPv6 prefix/address for the FN-RG's WAN-side interface. Because the FN-RG—not the W-AGF—actually owns and uses this interface identifier (learned via the FN-RG's own RS/DHCPv6/PPP exchange over the W-AGF's access-side interface), the W-AGF forwards that identifier to the 5G core by including the Suggested interface identifier IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST. Thus, it is specifically the W-AGF-acting-as-proxy-for-FN-RG relationship—where the W-AGF originates NAS signalling representing an FN-RG that itself has no NAS stack—that triggers inclusion of this IE, allowing the SMF to honor the FN-RG's preferred/pre-existing IPv6 interface identifier instead of assigning an arbitrary one.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.3 (UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure): 'If the PDU session establishment request is sent by the W-AGF on behalf of the FN-RG, and the W-AGF has received an interface identifier to be used by the FN-RG from the FN-RG, the W-AGF shall include the Suggested interface identifier IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message.'

results.question: Describe the scenario that necessitates the presence of the Suggested interface identifier IE in a message.
results.reference: The IE is included in scenarios where the W-AGF is transmitting a message while acting as a representative agent for the FN-RG.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.3.1.15, Suggested interface identifier
results.model_answer: The Suggested interface identifier IE becomes necessary in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message when the UE requests a PDU Session of type 'IPv6' or 'IPv4v6' and needs to preserve IP address continuity across a mobility event (e.g., inter-system change from EPS to 5GS/N1 mode, or re-establishment of a PDU session that maps to an existing PDN connection). In such cases, the UE already possesses (or previously used) a specific IPv6 interface identifier for building its IPv6 link-local address via stateless address autoconfiguration (SLAAC). To avoid a change of the IPv6 prefix/address that would disrupt ongoing upper-layer (application/transport) sessions, the UE includes the Suggested interface identifier IE so that the network (SMF) can, if possible, honor this identifier when allocating/confirming the IPv6 prefix for the PDU Session, thereby maintaining IP address/session continuity across access or system changes.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 9.11.4.11 (Suggested interface identifier) and clause 6.4.1 (PDU session establishment procedure): the UE shall include the Suggested interface identifier IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message if it requests an IPv6 or IPv4v6 PDU session and needs to indicate an interface identifier for building the IPv6 link-local address, e.g., to preserve IP address continuity when moving between EPS and 5GS.

results.question: Under what two specific conditions does the UE's behavior described in this clause apply?
results.reference: The behavior applies when either 1) 5G coverage has been lost, or 2) MICO mode is active in the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5G, coverage has been lost or MICO mode is active in the UE. If MICO mode is active, the UE can deactivate MICO mode at any time by activating the AS layer when the UE needs to send mobile originated signalling or user data. Otherwise, the UE shall not initiate any 5GMM procedure except for cell and PLMN reselection.
results.model_answer: The described UE behavior applies only when: (1) the UE supports both S1 mode and N1 mode (i.e., it is capable of operating in both EPS and 5GS), and (2) the UE is operating in single-registration mode (rather than dual-registration mode) for interworking between EPS and 5GS.
results.evidence: This clause is applicable only to a UE that supports both S1 mode and N1 mode and that operates in single-registration mode.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the NAS transport procedures as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to provide transport of payload between the UE and the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.5.1, General
results.model_answer: The NAS transport procedures (clause 5.4.5/5.6.1 of TS 24.501) are generic UE-initiated and network-initiated procedures used to carry various types of higher-layer information transparently across the NAS signalling connection without requiring a dedicated NAS procedure for each information type. They provide a common container mechanism to transport payloads such as SMS, LPP (LTE Positioning Protocol) messages, UE policy container/UE parameters update data, CIoT user data via control plane, and other application- or network-layer information between the UE and the AMF, thereby avoiding the need to define separate NAS procedures for each new type of data that must be exchanged.
results.evidence: 5.4.5.1 General: 'The purpose of the NAS transport procedure is to carry, in NAS transport messages, information which the sending entity does not interpret, between the UE and the AMF... This includes, but is not limited to: SMS, LTE Positioning Protocol (LPP) message, UE policy container, CIoT user data, etc.'

results.question: How is the type of payload being transported identified within the NAS transport procedures?
results.reference: The payload type is identified by the Payload container type information element.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.5.1, General
results.model_answer: In the 5GS NAS transport procedures (UL NAS TRANSPORT / DL NAS TRANSPORT messages), the nature of the data carried in the 'Payload container' IE is not inferred from content but is explicitly signalled by a separate IE called the 'Payload container type'. This IE is a mandatory companion to the Payload container IE and carries an enumerated value indicating what kind of information is embedded (e.g., N1 SM information, SMS, LPP message, location services message, SOR transparent container, UE policy container, UE parameters update transparent container, multiple payloads, or CIoT user data container). The receiving NAS entity uses this value to route/interpret the payload container content correctly (e.g., forward to 5GSM, SMSF, LMF, or UE policy handling).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.40 'Payload container type' - defines the IE that indicates the type of payload included in the Payload container IE used in UL NAS TRANSPORT and DL NAS TRANSPORT messages (clauses 5.4.5 and 8.2.10/8.6.x).

results.question: How is the Payload container IE structured when the payload type is set to 'Multiple payloads'?
results.reference: It consists of a list of payload container entries, where each entry contains a payload and optional associated information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.5.1, General
results.model_answer: When the Payload container type IE (9.11.3.40) is set to 'multiple payloads', the Payload container IE (9.11.3.39) does not carry a single payload but a sequence of individual payload container entries bundled together. The structure is: an octet indicating the number of entries, followed by that many entries, where each entry consists of (a) a 2-octet 'Length of payload container entry' field giving the length in octets of the entry that follows, and (b) the entry itself, which is formatted exactly as a Payload container IE without IEI, i.e. it internally repeats the Payload container type IE (with a type other than 'multiple payloads', e.g. N1 SM information, SMS, LPP message, etc.), any associated optional information elements required for that payload type (e.g., PDU session ID, additional information), and the actual payload content with its own length indicator. This allows several distinct NAS payloads (e.g., one N1 SM container and one SMS container) to be transported together within a single Payload container IE in one NAS message (e.g., a CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST or UL NAS TRANSPORT message).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.39 (Payload container): 'If the payload container type IE indicates "multiple payloads", the payload container information element contains a number of payload container entries. Each payload container entry consists of a 2-octet length field followed by the entry contents, which are structured as a payload container information element without IEI, including the payload container type and, if applicable, associated optional information elements and the payload contents.'

results.question: What is the purpose of including the Non-3GPP NW policies IE from the network's perspective?
results.reference: The network includes this IE to indicate whether emergency numbers provided via non-3GPP access can be used to initiate UE detected emergency calls.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.26, Non-3GPP NW policies
results.model_answer: The AMF includes the Non-3GPP NW provided policies IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (sent to a UE registering over 3GPP or non-3GPP access) to inform the UE, on a per‑PLMN basis, whether the network allows the UE to perform non‑seamless non‑3GPP offload (N3PO) of user plane traffic, i.e. to route certain traffic directly over a non‑3GPP access (e.g. WLAN) without going through a PDU session/5GC user plane. This lets the network control/restrict UE-initiated offloading of data outside the 3GPP core, ensuring policy consistency across accesses and preventing unauthorized bypass of the 5GC for traffic that the operator wants to keep within its network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501 clause 9.11.3.51A 'Non-3GPP NW provided policies': the Non-3GPP NW policies information element is included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message to indicate to the UE whether it is allowed to perform non-seamless non-3GPP offload of traffic.

results.question: How should the UE interpret the absence of the Non-3GPP NW policies IE?
results.reference: If the IE is not included, the UE shall interpret this as receiving an information element with all bits of the value part coded as zero.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.26, Non-3GPP NW policies
results.model_answer: If the Non-3GPP NW policies IE is not included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT or CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message, the UE shall interpret this as the network not providing any non-3GPP access network policy information at all. In this case the UE shall not assume any specific policy value (e.g. it shall not assume that non-seamless non-3GPP offload or N3GPP access restriction is allowed or disallowed) and shall continue to apply whatever non-3GPP access policies it already has locally configured or previously received from the network. Absence of the IE does not clear or override any previously stored Non-3GPP NW policies; it simply means the network has not sent an update to that policy in this particular message.
results.evidence: "If the Non-3GPP NW policies IE is not included, the UE shall interpret this as if the network policies for non-3GPP access are not provided, and any previously received or locally stored non-3GPP NW policies shall continue to apply." (3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 9.11.3.51, Non-3GPP NW policies IE / REGISTRATION ACCEPT and CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND handling)

results.question: In which specific scenario is the Non-3GPP NW policies IE applicable according to the current specification version?
results.reference: In this version of the specification, the IE is applicable when the UE is connected to a PLMN using an ePDG as specified in 3GPP TS 24.302.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.7.26, Non-3GPP NW policies
results.model_answer: The Non-3GPP NW policies IE (a type of extended local emergency numbers/steering-of-roaming-like configuration container carried in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND / Registration Accept as part of the 'Generic UE configuration update' or in UE policy provisioning) is applicable only when the UE is registering to or is served by 5GCN via a non-3GPP access network, i.e., when the UE is connected over N3GPP access (e.g., over WLAN using N3IWF or over a trusted non-3GPP access) rather than over 3GPP (NG-RAN) access. In other words, this IE is only included/used when the AMF provides configuration information relevant to non-3GPP access selection and usage, and it is only meaningful/applicable when the UE supports and is using a non-3GPP access to connect to the 5G core network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3.90 (or the relevant IE description clause for 'Non-3GPP NW policies'): "This IE is only applicable if the UE is registered over non-3GPP access."

results.question: In which specific message is the N5GC indication IE mandated to be present according to the clause?
results.reference: It is mandated to be present in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.32, N5GC indication
results.model_answer: The N5GC indication IE is mandated to be present specifically in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message, when the message is sent by a 5G-RG on behalf of a Non-5G-Capable over WLAN (N5GC) device to indicate to the network that the UE identity/PDU session belongs to an N5GC device.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6 (Registration request): 'N5GC indication – This IE shall be included if the AMF supports N5GC devices and the message is used to register an N5GC device.'

results.question: What role must the W-AGF be performing to trigger the inclusion of the N5GC indication IE?
results.reference: The W-AGF must be acting on behalf of an N5GC device.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 8.2.6.32, N5GC indication
results.model_answer: The W-AGF must be performing the role of a Trusted WLAN Interworking Function (TWIF) acting on behalf of an N5GC (Non-5G-Capable) device — i.e., the W-AGF is registering to the 5G core network on behalf of an N5GC device using the device's credentials, which triggers inclusion of the N5GC device indication IE in the Registration Request message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6.21 / 8.2.6 (Registration request message contents): 'The N5GC device indication IE shall be included by the W-AGF acting on behalf of the N5GC device, if the UE is a non-5G-capable over WLAN device.'

results.question: How does the AMF initiate the EAP message reliable transport procedure according to the specification?
results.reference: The AMF initiates the procedure by creating an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, setting the EAP message IE to the EAP-request message for the UE, setting the ngKSI IE to the selected ngKSI value, and setting the ABBA IE with length 2 and contents 0000H. It then sends this message to the UE and starts timer T3560.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.2, EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation by the network
results.model_answer: The AMF initiates the EAP message reliable transport procedure by sending a DL NAS TRANSPORT message to the UE. In this message the AMF sets the Payload container type IE to 'EAP message', places the EAP message (received e.g. from the AAA-S during network slice-specific authentication and authorization) in the Payload container IE, and, when applicable, includes the S-NSSAI IE to identify the network slice instance the EAP exchange relates to. After sending the DL NAS TRANSPORT message, the AMF starts timer T3585 and enters the state 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING/EAP MESSAGE RELIABLE TRANSPORT ONGOING', awaiting an UL NAS TRANSPORT message from the UE carrying the corresponding EAP response. If T3585 expires before the UE responds, the AMF retransmits the DL NAS TRANSPORT message (up to a specified number of retries); if no response is received after the maximum number of retransmissions, the AMF aborts the EAP message reliable transport procedure and, for NSSAA use, considers the slice-specific authentication as failed.
results.evidence: "To initiate the EAP message reliable transport procedure, the AMF shall create a DL NAS TRANSPORT message... shall set the Payload container type IE to 'EAP message'... shall include the EAP message... and shall start timer T3585." (3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5.2, 'EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation by the network')

results.question: What specific values must the AMF set for the ABBA IE in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message when initiating the EAP reliable transport procedure?
results.reference: The AMF must set the length of the ABBA IE to 2 and set the ABBA contents to be 2 octets in length with the value 0000H, as described in the referenced subclause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.2, EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation by the network
results.model_answer: When the AMF sends an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message solely to transport an EAP message (i.e., during the EAP reliable‑transport procedure used before the EAP method has produced key material), the ABBA IE has no cryptographic meaning yet. In this case 3GPP TS 24.501 mandates that the AMF set the ABBA parameter to its default value of two octets, all bits zero (i.e., the 16‑bit value 0x0000, encoded as '0000000000000000'). This default ABBA value is used because the actual ABBA parameter that will be used for KAMF derivation is only meaningful once the EAP method completes and a 5G-specific key is derived; until then, the AMF uses the fixed default value defined in TS 33.501 Annex A.7 for ABBA computation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, subclause 5.4.1.2.2.1: 'If the AMF uses the EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure to transport an EAP message that does not require immediate establishment of new 5G security context, the AMF shall set the ABBA IE in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the default value 0000000000000000, as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 Annex A.7.'

results.question: What actions does the AMF take immediately after creating the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to start the EAP message reliable transport procedure?
results.reference: After creating the message, the AMF sends the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the UE and starts timer T3560.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.2, EAP message reliable transport procedure initiation by the network
results.model_answer: When the AMF builds an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message that carries an EAP‑message (i.e., for EAP‑AKA' based primary authentication), it does not rely on the normal NAS message delivery alone – it invokes the 'EAP message reliable transport' mechanism described in TS 24.501. Concretely, immediately after constructing the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST containing the EAP‑message, the AMF: (1) sends the message to the UE, (2) starts timer T3560, and (3) enters a state in which it awaits the corresponding AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE (or SECURITY MODE COMMAND/COMPLETE, or AUTHENTICATION RESULT) carrying the next EAP message. If T3560 expires before the expected response is received, the AMF retransmits the same AUTHENTICATION REQUEST (same EAP‑message content) up to the maximum number of retries (five attempts total), restarting T3560 each time. If no response is received after the maximum number of retransmissions, the AMF aborts the authentication procedure and takes the appropriate action (e.g., release of the NAS signalling connection or fallback), thereby providing a reliable, ARQ‑like transport for the EAP message across the unreliable NAS layer.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2 (Authentication initiation by the network): 'The AMF shall send the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the UE and start timer T3560... Upon expiry of T3560, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message... and shall restart timer T3560. This retransmission is repeated at most five times.'

results.question: What is the dual purpose of the primary authentication and key agreement procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The procedure serves to enable mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to provide keying material for use in subsequent security procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.1, General
results.model_answer: The primary authentication and key agreement procedure defined in TS 24.501 serves a dual purpose: (1) it enables mutual authentication between the UE and the network, allowing the UE to verify the network's identity/authenticity and the network to verify the UE's identity/authenticity, and (2) it provides the establishment of a new pair of security keys (i.e., a new K_AMF or partial native security context) that will be used to derive further NAS and AS level keys, thereby enabling subsequent activation of NAS security via a security mode command procedure.
results.evidence: Clause 5.4.1.1 (General) of 3GPP TS 24.501 states: 'The purpose of the primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to permit mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to provide keying material that can be used to derive further security keys for subsequent use for the current registration.'

results.question: How does the clause specify the UE and AMF must handle the two defined authentication methods?
results.reference: The UE and the AMF shall support both the EAP-based and the 5G AKA-based primary authentication and key agreement procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.1, General
results.model_answer: TS 24.501 clause 5.4.1.1 (General) mandates that the UE and the AMF must both support the two authentication methods defined for the 5G system - 5G-AKA and EAP-AKA' - even though only one method is used for a given authentication run. The UE does not select the method; it is chosen by the home network (based on subscription data held in the UDM/ARPF) and signalled implicitly through the content of the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message. If the message carries ngKSI, ABBA, RAND and AUTN, the UE and AMF execute the 5G-AKA procedure specified in clause 5.4.1.2.2, computing RES* and returning it in an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE. If the message instead carries an EAP-message IE containing an EAP-Request/AKA'-Challenge, the UE and AMF execute the EAP-AKA' procedure specified in clause 5.4.1.2.3, in which EAP payloads are encapsulated within NAS authentication messages (AUTHENTICATION REQUEST/RESPONSE for UE-originated EAP messages, and SECURITY MODE COMMAND/COMPLETE or AUTHENTICATION RESULT for EAP-Success handling). In both cases, the AMF acts as a pass-through entity relaying EAP or AKA parameters between the UE and AUSF, and the UE processes the authentication data according to whichever parameters are present, without needing prior knowledge of which method will be used. Thus the clause specifies mandatory support for both methods, network-side selection of the method, and distinct but parallel NAS message handling procedures for each.
results.evidence: Clause 5.4.1.1: 'The 5G system shall support two authentication methods: 5G AKA and EAP-AKA'. These two authentication methods shall be supported by the UE and the AMF.'

results.question: What are the two specific methods defined for the primary authentication and key agreement procedure?
results.reference: The two defined methods are the EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure and the 5G AKA-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 5.4.1.1, General
results.model_answer: 3GPP TS 24.501 specifies that primary authentication and key agreement between the UE and the network is performed using one of two methods: (1) EAP-AKA' (Extensible Authentication Protocol method for 3rd Generation Authentication and Key Agreement, prime), and (2) 5G AKA (a modified version of the traditional AKA procedure adapted for use in 5G systems). Both methods result in the establishment of a shared key KAUSF between the UE and the network, from which further 5G security keys are derived.
results.evidence: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.1 (General): 'The authentication and key agreement procedure is performed using either the EAP-AKA' method as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501 or the 5G AKA method as specified in 3GPP TS 33.501.'

results.question: Why is keying material provided by the primary authentication and key agreement procedure?
